title: Morning Group Meditation
location: Ananda Temple in Beaverton, 4855 SW Watson Avenue, Beaverton, Oregon, 97005, United States
description:
Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: Run & Chug!
description:
Portland Fun Run
The route will be posted soon! In the meantime, here are some FAQs:

**Where do I find the group?**
We typically meet up right outside the bar! We rotate through a variety of bars and breweries. Check out our past events to see what places we typically go to.

**What is the average pace of the group?**
There is a wide range of paces that varies week-to-week, but typically most people are between 7:30 - 10 minute miles. We welcome all runners, regardless of pace (the #1 goal our group is to make new friends, not break records), but we advise making sure you are comfortable with the route if you are worried you might be slower than this range, just so you don’t get lost.

* Need a running buddy or want to check if anyone else in the group is running your pace? Feel free to message Erin to coordinate this! Please send any messages by Tuesday evening the day before we meet 😊

**What time does the group actually start running?**
We suggest runners arrive around 6:55pm, but we do not actually start running until 7:05pm.

**When is the route posted?**
The route is posted typically Tuesday night or Wednesday morning.
I don’t have a car, what do I do with my belongings while I’m running?
One option is to wear a running belt to keep keys, ID, credit card, etc. on you while you run, but if you show up a little early, you can often find someone who is willing to put your jacket or other belongings in their car for you during the run.

**What should I bring?**
Make sure to bring your ID and credit card/cash for the bar. Additionally, in the winter, we recommend bringing a light to run with and wearing something reflective. Lastly, we are sometimes outside for drinks, depending on the location, so it’s a good idea to bring a jacket.

description:

The Mt. Hood Jazz Festival kicks off its five-day immersion into the jazz culture at The Old Church! This first event includes professional performances by world-renowned artists.

In celebration of the centennial of John Coltrane and Miles Davis, pianist Emmet Cohen brings together an all-star quintet to explore the fundamental questions that shaped their artistry: Why are we here? What are we reaching for? Where does the music take us?

title: Morning Group Meditation
location: Ananda Temple in Beaverton, 4855 SW Watson Avenue, Beaverton, Oregon, 97005, United States
description:
Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. title: Enduring Impressions: Contemporary Woodblock Prints
location: Portland Japanese Garden, 611 SW Kingston Ave., Portland, OR, 97205
description:
Step into a world where nature-themed prints meet Portland Japanese Garden’s springtime vibrance in Enduring Impressions: Contemporary Woodblock Prints. Featuring the art of mokuhanga (木版画), Japanese-style woodblock printmaking, this exhibition reveals how a centuries-old tradition is experiencing a contemporary revival as artists around the world use the quiet power and unique characteristics of woodblock printmaking to create captivating works of art.
Mokuhanga has been embraced as an environmentally friendly art form that uses wood, water-based pigments, and paper made from plant fibers. The exhibition’s featured artists are among the growing international movement where meticulously crafted art prints incorporating these traditional tools and techniques are complemented by alternative printmaking technologies and strategies for contemporary expression. This exhibition marks the Garden’s first collaboration with the Honolulu Museum of Art and is co-curated by Stephen Salel, the Museum’s Curator of Japanese Art. Across the galleries at Portland Japanese Garden, Enduring Impressions presents an eclectic range of contemporary prints, alongside a behind-the-scenes look at the process, history and future of this iconic art form.

The so-called "Banach-Tarski paradox" is a kind of mathematical magic trick, the performance of which goes as follows: the mathemagician takes a solid 3 dimensional ball, decomposes it into finitely many pieces, and then reassembles these pieces using only ordinary Euclidean translations and rotations into two complete copies of the original ball. In clear violation of the magician's code, I will explain the trick by giving an accessible proof of this remarkable fact, and discuss the resolution of this apparent "paradox" in 3 dimensional geometry.

title: The Last Letter of 'Red' Condori: Resistance in the Archives of Cold War Bolivia
location: Psychology, 105
description:
In June 1967, a miner named Casildo Condori wrote a birthday letter to his wife Nancy from the rearguard of Che Guevara’s guerrilla column. When he died in a fire fight with the Bolivian army a few days later, the soldiers kept the letter and the money he sent home. Nancy, fearing Casildo had abandoned their daughter, eventually turned to the courts to track her husband down. Che’s diary barely mentions the young miner and a Cuban memorial uses the wrong name, but Casildo was more than a footnote in the Cold War. In this talk, I use an unexpected archive: the family courts of a small mining city, to put Nancy, Casildo, and their peers in the center of their own revolutionary struggle to protect working families and the keep resistance alive in the face of a violent state and a harsh physical landscape.

Elena McGrath is Assistant Professor of History and Assistant Dean of Studies at Union College in Schenectady, New York. Her research interests, which started with a 2006 Reed History thesis advised by David Garrett, include race, gender, and revolution in the Andes. She received her PhD in Latin American History from the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 2016 and her first book, The Limits of Revolution: Worker Citizens in a Bolivian Mining City, was published by the University of Texas Press in March.

title: Spring Women's Retreat
description:
Come away to the sea.

Join us for a nourishing weekend retreat on the Oregon Coast — a gathering of women devotees of Yogananda, coming together to breathe, create, move, and simply be in one another's company.

The ocean has always been a place of return. Let its rhythms carry you back to yourself.

ABOUT THE RETREAT

This retreat is an invitation to slow down and go inward — supported by the prana of the Pacific, the warmth of Sangha sisterhood, and a spacious weekend away from the demands of daily life.

Together we'll explore:

Meditation — Daily group meditation to deepen your practice and reconnect with Master's teachings in a space held by fellow devotees.

Yoga — Daily Ananda yoga sessions to open the body, quiet the mind, and move prana with intention.

Art — Creative expression as spiritual practice. No experience needed — only a willingness to play, discover, and let something new come through.

Community — Meals cooked and shared, stories exchanged, laughter, silence, and the particular joy of being truly known by women who walk the same path.

THE DETAILS

Dates: Weekend of April 24, 2025

Location: Oregon Coast (Rockaway Beach)

The venue: Rockaway Beach House

Open to: Women devotees of Yogananda

Capacity: 15 women (limited enrollment)

Sleeping arrangements:  8 shared bedrooms

All meals included — vegetarian, lovingly prepared

Investment: $250 per person

Transportation:  Carpooling can be arranged

THE FOOD

All meals are included and entirely vegetarian — nourishing, fresh, and prepared with care. Gluten Free and Vegan options available upon request. From morning chai to evening dinner, food is part of the retreat experience. Come hungry. Leave restored.

WHO THIS IS FOR

This retreat is for you if you're longing to:

Reconnect with your spiritual practices
Be in community with women who understand the Ananda path
Experience the restorative prana of the ocean
Explore creativity as a form of devotion
Rest, replenish, and return home renewed

Space is limited to 15 women. If you feel the call, we'd love to have you with us.

Contact Gita Matlock (gitamcgilloway@gmail.com) or

Melissa Heart (melissa27heart@gmail.com) if you have questions.

6:15 - doors are open

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

title: Identifying and Understanding Autism in Women: Assessment Through Intervention (Online)
location: Online
description: This presentation for mental health practitioners aims to deepen understanding of how autism and related forms of neurodivergence present in girls and women, and to support more accurate, ethical, and affirming identification and care.  Autism is a complex and multifaceted form of neurodivergence, encompassing a wide range of traits that can present differently across individuals, contexts, and developmental stages. The most widely-recognized presentation of autism is generally based on research conducted on white, middle- to upper-class males, often emphasizing conventionally "masculine" interests and behaviors.  As a result, much of the diagnostic criteria for autism and ADHD in the DSM does not capture how neurodivergence presents in girls, women, transgender and nonbinary individuals, and people of color.Many autistic females and gender-diverse individuals are misdiagnosed, overlooked, or misunderstood in childhood, with their traits minimized, masked, or misinterpreted as behavioral or emotional difficulties rather than recognized as neurodevelopmental differences.  Recent research finds that nearly 80% of autistic females are undiagnosed as of the age of 18.  This presentation will explore the following:Neurodivergence in girls and women: How traits in females both align with and diverge from DSM criteria, including differences in cognitive and sensory processing, executive functioning, social cognition, communication, and the influence of gendered expectations on identification    Masking and it's impact: What is it, how does it develop, and its long- and short- term consequences    Assessment and referral: Best practices, including timing, developmentally sensitive testing, ethical and equity-informed considerations, and neurodiversity-affirming language, and Theory of Mind     Treatment and Support: Nervous system–informed, strengths-based interventions that support unmasking and self-understanding, prevent autistic burnout, and promote sustainable functioning through individualized, neurodiversity-affirming treatment plans      This workshop may meet the OBLPCT Cultural Competence Continuing Education requirement. Click here for more information (http://www.oregon.gov/oblpct/Pages/CCCE.aspx)Details & RegistrationRegistration for this workshop is now closedDate and Time: Friday, April 24, 2026, 9 a.m.-2 p.m., PT, OnlinePresenter: Ashley Taylor, PsyDCost and Credits: $105, includes 4 CEUs. $45 student rate. GSEC Alumni and Adjuncts save 20%  No-cost registration available for GSEC Mental Health Clinical Supervisors, Faculty, and Staff. Email cce@lclark.edu (mailto:cce@lclark.ed) with your request to register.Accessibility: We are committed to making our events accessible to all needs and abilities. When registering, please let us know your access needs. Contact us at 503-768-6040 or cce@lclark.edu (mailto:cce@lclark.edu) with questions.Please note: Discounted ‘Student Rate’ registrations are for current students only and do not include continuing education credit (CEU/PDUs)About the PresenterDr. Ashley Taylor is a licensed clinical psychologist in California and Washington State, author, and founder of Wonder Tree Developmental Psychology. She specializes in providing comprehensive evaluations through a reflective, neurodiversity affirming lens. She has provided high quality care to those with neurodivergence for over 15 years. Dr. Taylor lives in Southwest Washington with her husband and two boys. She has recently become a yoga teacher and enjoys spending time with her family, pets, going hiking, snowboarding, and doing yoga. Wonder Tree Developmental Psychology has locations in Vancouver, Washington and Pasadena, California, providing an excellent team of developmental psychologists, occupational therapists, and educational specialists that support developmental across the lifespan.New workshops and trainings are added to our calendar regularly. For the latest on professional development related to your specific interests, sign up for our mailing list! (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/4735441)

title: Gentle Ananda Yoga with Melissa
location: Ananda Portland Temple, 4855 SW Watson Ave, Beaverton, OR, 97005, United States
description:
This class is ideal for beginners, those recovering from injury, or anyone seeking a deeply restorative practice. It’s less about “doing” and more about “being,” with props acting as companions to guide the body into ease.

Class Atmosphere

Lighting & Ambiance: Soft, warm lighting with calming music or silence to encourage relaxation.
Pace: Slow, mindful transitions with long holds to allow the body to settle.
Focus: Creating comfort, stability, and spaciousness in each posture.

Props & Supports

Bolsters & Pillows: Used to support the spine or to cushion knees in seated poses.
Blankets: Folded for extra padding under joints or rolled to elevate hips.
Blocks: Provide height and stability in standing poses or gentle forward folds.
Straps: Assist in reaching without strain, especially in hamstring stretches or shoulder openers.
Chairs: Offer support for balance postures or seated variations.

Flow of the Class

Centering: Begin by focusing on breath awareness.
Gentle Warm-Up
Ananda Poses: supported standing poses like warrior variations with a chair or block.
Relaxation: Savasana with props.
Guided meditation with visualization

Benefits

Physical: Relieves tension, supports joints, encourages gentle mobility.
Mental: Reduces stress, cultivates mindfulness, enhances body awareness.
Emotional: Creates a safe, nurturing environment for release and renewal.

Ananda Yoga® is inherently gentle and our instructors encourage and support appropriate modifications so all bodies can participate safely. Come early to class and speak with the instructor about your needs.
$15.00 per class
$10.00 per class:  Senior discount for 60 years old +

Drop-ins welcome. Preregister and prepayment optional.

Melissa Heart has been teaching Ananda Yoga since 2012 as a certified Ananda Yoga instructor. She’s been with Ananda Portland since 2007 and has served in many capacities at the temple. Currently she serves as a member of the ministry team, manager of the temple and coordinator for Education for Life Outreach Programs.

***************************************************************************
Testimonial from Lori Arveson, student:
"I have been practicing Ananda Yoga for several years, and it has become a deeply inward and centering experience for me. The postures are held with mindful awareness, each accompanied by a silent affirmation that gently guides my attention within. As I move through the poses, my mind settles and the practice becomes a form of moving meditation.
Melissa brings a soft, grounded presence to each class. She begins by inviting us into stillness, seated in meditation with uplifting Ananda music, and gently leads us through pranayama. The class closes with a few moments of silent meditation, allowing everything to integrate. By the end of each session, I feel both deeply relaxed and quietly energized, carrying a sense of calm with me beyond the mat."
 

Review of Ananda Yoga – Beaverton OR.
From: Rick Cady - Tualatin, OR.

"As a current student of Ayurveda, I had been looking to complement my studies with a Yoga tradition that would support the ideals espoused by the ancients related to the Yoga sciences. Given that the Western model of Yoga tends toward only a focus on the physical aspects of the practice, I was happy to find a more traditional practice of Hatha Yoga through the Ananda Temple here in Beaverton, OR. Teacher Melissa Heart brings this practice to life with her unique and effective teaching style with an emphasis on being conscious and still as we move into poses, hold the pose, and come out of the pose. This practice emphasizes utilizing the poses to relax the body and be aware of our state of mind to ultimately prepare for meditation. Melissa is a gem that I am grateful to have met, as you can feel her love for the practice and desire to share it with others. On a physical level, I had been diagnosed many years ago with a Lumbar spine defect that had given me significant pain and limitations for several decades, and this practice has made me virtually pain free in about 3 months. A true miracle. I am forever grateful and will be a lifetime supporter of Melissa and Ananda Yoga."

title: Biology SPARKLE Talks: Seniors Presenting About (their) Research, Knowledge, Learning, & Efforts
location: Biology, 19
description:
Join the Biology department as seniors share their thesis research and discuss their their experiences throughout their thesis journey.

Andrew Nguyen ‘26 - Neuroscience, Cerveny Lab

“Munchy Microglia - Cells that Eat Brainz”

Microglia are neuroimmune cells of the central nervous system that are key players in neuroinflammation. Within the developing zebrafish brain, phagocytic microglia can be observed responding to neuron death caused by developmental apoptosis and surgical insults. By comparing how phagocytic microglia behave under normal or injured developmental contexts, my thesis investigates how these cells coordinate their behaviors through space and time.

Jolie Jaffe ‘26 - Biology, Fey Lab

“The Effects of Noise Pollution on the Calling Patterns of The Northern Red Legged Frog (Rana aurora)”

I used playback experiments and Underwater Passive Acoustic Monitoring techniques to understand how noise pollution impacts the Northern Red-Legged Frog (Rana aurora) at Oaks Bottom Wildlife Refuge.

Paris Harrell ‘26 - Biology, Applewhite Lab

“Exploring the Effects of Maternal Recovered Acute Kidney Injury on Offspring Neurological Development”

In a mouse model of rhabdomyolysis-induced acute kidney injury (RIAKI), breeding mice with a history of recovered RIAKI resulted in dams with impaired kidney function during pregnancy. Offspring were born at term but were 3 times more likely to die in the pre-weaning period and exhibited far 5x higher rates of spontaneous hydrocephalus in adulthood. This project’s goal is to identify any differences in the vascular and immunological profile of the adult offspring brain using immunostaining techniques in order to identify potential developmental origins of disease in offspring of parents with recovered RIAKI.

title: PubMed Essentials: Save Time and Find Better Results
location: Virtual
description:
Make the most of PubMed for your research! This hands-on workshop will introduce strategies for efficient and effective searching, helping you save time and find higher-quality evidence. You'll learn how to use PubMed to construct more precise searches with more relevant results. We will also talk about methods to mitigate biases in your search, and some tips on leveraging AI to help enrich your search strategy. Whether you are new to information research or looking to sharpen your search expertise, this session will equip you with practical skills to improve your research process.

By the end of this session, learners will be able to:

Use features of PubMed for efficient and effective searching, including crafting advanced Boolean queries
Use PubMed accounts to save searches and create search alerts
Evaluate contextual authority and bias in PubMed and related tools and revise searches to mitigate those biases

This workshop will be recorded, and the recording will be shared with all registered attendees after the session. If you cannot make the workshop date and time, you are welcome to register in order to receive a copy of the recording.

location: Lan Su Chinese Garden, 239 NW Everett Street, Portland, Oregon, 97209
description:
Instructor | Tickets | Series Schedule | Parking

Enjoy a blossom-filled afternoon at the beautiful Lan Su Chinese Garden with the return of Steep & Paint. With all materials provided and admission included, all you need to bring is yourself!

We’re bringing this series back by popular demand and newly reimagined in partnership with the Oregon Botanical Artists (OBA). This immersive afternoon experience invites you to slow down, look closely, and connect with plants through tea, conversation, and hands-on art-making. Our August 14 Lotus session with Zebith Thalden will use colored pencils as the medium.

Each session weaves together horticulture, tea culture, and botanical art in a relaxed, welcoming setting:

Learn the plant up close: A Lan Su gardener leads a close-up botanical show-and-tell, sharing seasonal plant facts, cultural stories, and growing insights.

Taste the season: Enjoy a sampling of seasonal teas from Yun Shui Teahouse.

Create botanical art: An OBA artist guides a full botanical art class inspired by the featured plant.

Whether you’re returning to Steep & Paint or joining for the first time, this refreshed program offers an even richer way to experience Lan Su. Bring a friend with you and let’s Steep & Paint together!

Meet the Instructor: Rhiannon Leonard

“Poppy” by Rhiannon Leonard

Rhiannon Leonard is passionate about the intersection of art & botany and explores the emotional benefits of slowing down to draw the plants around us. Teaching for over 15 years in Portland, she is dedicated to making her classes accessible through community education & lower cost programming.

Meet Our Partner: Oregon Botanical Artists (OBA)

Oregon Botanical Artists is a nonprofit organization dedicated to promoting contemporary botanical art while honoring its long-standing traditions. Founded in 2012, the organization supports a diverse community of artists who celebrate the beauty and diversity of plant life through detailed and scientifically informed artwork. Oregon Botanical Artists is affiliated with the American Society of Botanical Artists as an Artists Circle.

title: Decompress + Connect Meditation Group
description:
Decompress + Connect Meditation Group
Decompress and connect at the end of your work week with meditation practice and community. This event is in partnership with the Young Meditators Group of Portland.

This open session offers 20 minutes of silent meditation followed by a meditative talking circle practice, and the opportunity to connect and socialize afterwards at a local pub.

**No experience required, and meditators of all traditions are welcome.**
**Cushions will be provided but feel free to bring your own.**

**SCHEDULE**

**6:30 – 7:00PM Silent Meditation**
Silent meditation practice (you are welcome to practice a silent meditation of your choosing)

**7:00 – 7:25PM Meditative Talking Circle**
Resting on the foundation of meditation practice, this talking circle practice expands to include others in the circle. While maintaining a meditation practice, members of the circle are welcome to speak from the present moment, though speaking is not required to participate. Instructions will be provided at the beginning so please arrive on time for this part of the practice.

**7:25PM Closing and Social**
There will be some time after group to connect after practice, after which the group may choose to go out for drinks and snacks at a nearby pub within walking distance.

This is a 'by donation' event. Suggested donation amount $3-10: [Please Donate Here](https://www.paypal.com/donate?hosted_button_id=PPCNJX8KYKY42)

If you are a regular member, please consider signing up for a monthly donation- it helps make this group sustainable!

title: Ethical Considerations in Psychedelic-Assisted Psychotherapy (In-Person)
location: Lewis & Clark Graduate School, TBA
description: This course offers an overview of the integration aspect of psychedelic-assisted therapy, and examines ethical considerations that can impact the overall and long-term experience of clients receiving treatment.  We will focus on integration as an intentional process of bringing awareness to the impact of the psychedelic experience and applying it to one's life in ways that can be transformative.  Ethical issues, harm reduction interventions in psychedelic-assisted therapy practices, and anthropocentric and biocentric perspectives on working with psychedelic medicines in therapy will be discussed.Following the completion of this course, participants should have a better understanding of:How to apply tools to conceptualize and facilitate integration practices.  Affirmative ethics and harm reduction frameworks, and how they apply to psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy.  Psychedelic-assisted psychotherapy from a biocentric perspective, which focuses on the relationship between humans, plant medicines, psychedelic medicines, and psychotherapy.  Integrating the diversity, equity, and inclusion dimensions of everyday life and clinical work into psychedelic therapy.  Course Details & RegistrationDates and Times: Saturday-Sunday, April 25-26, 2026, 9 a.m.-5:30 p.m.Location: Lewis & Clark Graduate School, Portland, OregonInstructors: Elizabeth Hoke, LMFT; and Veronica Vargas, LPCGraduate-level Continuing Education credit: CECP-866-01, 1 semester hour, $375We are committed to making our events accessible to all needs and abilities. If you have a disability that may impact your academic performance, you may request accommodations by meeting with the Office of Student Accessibility staff and submitting documentation on the Office of Student Accessibility website (/offices/student-accessibility/). Please be aware that the process for evaluation and implementation of accommodations could take 2-3 weeks, so please be in touch with the OSA as soon as possible. Email access@lclark.edu (mailto:access@lclark.edu) with any additional questions or concerns.About the Instructors Elizabeth Hoke, MFT is the Clinical Director of Liberation Institute in Portland where she supervises and provides psychoeducational trainings and workshops. She specializes in working with addiction recovery and ADHD, using a mix of theoretical tools rooted in somatic psychology and biocentric philosophies. Elizabeth co-facilitates ketamine-assisted psychotherapy sessions at Rainfall Medicine and co-leads addiction recovery support groups at Portland Psychedelic Society and the Rhizome. She has completed the 100-hour MDMA Therapy Training program through the Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Studies. Elizabeth also co-created the Entheogen Assisted Psychotherapy and Integration Training Series for licensed professionals at Lewis & Clark Graduate School Center for Community Engagement in 2021. Veronica Vargas, MA, LPC journeys alongside folks in their path towards healing, harmony, and contentment. She finds beauty in witnessing the unfolding of human potential, and cultivation of meaning. Her formal training is in counseling psychology with an emphasis in depth-psychotherapy. Depth-psychotherapy can be defined as a holistic approach that examines all aspects of a person's life, including dreams, art, fantasies, philosophies, and conscious thoughts. She was heavily influenced by the work of Swiss psychiatrist, Carl Gustav Jung. In her work as a licensed psychotherapist she assesses the whole person or family system by looking at relational and cultural systems; spirituality; personal and intergenerational trauma; systems of oppression; personal values and how they are or aren't reflected authentically in the person's life. She has a private practice in Portland, Oregon where she offers psychotherapy, dream work, and psychedelic integration therapy. .   New workshops and trainings are added to our calendar regularly. For the latest on professional development related to your specific interests, sign up for our mailing list! (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/4735441)

title: Fat Studies & Health at Every Size (Online)
location: Online
description: This course explores the interdisciplinary field of scholarship in Fat Studies that aims to debunk weight-centric misconceptions and countering mainstream narratives.  Participants will examine fat bias, fat shame and weight-based oppression as a social justice issue that intersects with other systems of oppression.  This course includes an introduction to the paradigm of Health At Every Size (HAES), a weight-neutral approach to health promotion that emphasizes size diversity, intuitive eating, and joyful movement. HAES is also an important paradigm in working with people who experience disordered eating.  This course is part of our Eating Disorders Certificate Program (https://graduate.lclark.edu/programs/continuing_education/certificates/eating_disorders/). Course Details & RegistrationDates & Times: Saturday-Sunday, April 25-26, 2026, 9 a.m.-5:30 p.m., PT, OnlineInstructor: Krystal Marcinkiewicz, MA, LPC, LMHCRegistration:Register online (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/4735425).Current Students and Certificate Candidates: CECP 835-02, 1 semester hour of Graduate Continuing Education Credit, $375. Email access@lclark.edu (mailto:access@lclark.edu) with any additional questions or concerns.About the InstructorKrystal Marcinkiewicz, MA, LPC, LMHC is a Licensed Professional Counselor and Clinical Supervisor, having earned her Masters Degree in Professional Mental Health Counseling from Lewis & Clark College in 2018. Drawing from an integrative feminist approach, her work is grounded in person-centered values, emphasizing authentic connection, and collaborative engagement. Her primary clinical focus is supporting clients in navigating identity development, body politics, neurodivergence, emotional codependency, highly sensitive personalities and other complex emotional experiences.  In addition to clinical work, Krystal is also passionate in training and mentoring emerging counselors. She is an adjunct professor, teaching a wide variety of graduate counseling courses with an underlying emphasis on counselor identity development, reflective practice, and cultivating professional resilience. title: Gladstone Arbor Day & Plant Sale
location: Gladstone Nature Park,18111 Webster Road, Gladstone, OR 97027, USA
description:
Join the Friends of Gladstone Nature Park on April 25, 2026 for our 10th Annual Arbor Day & Plant Sale in the Gladstone Nature Park, 18111 Webster Road in Gladstone.

The sale runs from 9am to 3pm and includes: Oregon native plants, vegetable starts, hanging baskets, perennials, kitchen herbs, mushroom grow-kits, free seeds for sharing, fruit and berry plants, local honey, tool sharpening, soil testing, free kids books, electronics recycling and concessions.

Many special plants from Willamette Valley nurseries will be featured. The Clackamas County Library will offer their free seed collection. Kraxberger Robotics team will recycle your electronics. Gladstone High School students will offer herbs from their greenhouse program. Gladstone Baseball Association will have refreshments to purchase to support their teams. We will have our beautiful hanging baskets for Mother’s Day again.

Are you doing a native garden or Backyard Habitat? We will have abundant varieties of native plants to get you started and experts on hand to advise you.

The event is free and parking is available at the LDS church at 8331 Cason Road, in Gladstone. Please use the crosswalk. The park is served by TriMet bus lines 31 & 32. Proceeds support restoration projects in the Gladstone Nature Park. A can or 2 of food for our local food bank is much appreciated!

For more information, contact: FriendsOfGladstoneNature@gmailcom mailto:FriendsOfGladstoneNature@gmailcom?subject=Plant%20sale .

Saturday, April 25, is Independent Bookstore Day! Come celebrate with us at 716 SE Grand Avenue from 9:00 a.m. – 8:00 p.m for a day full of books, community, festivity, and surprises!
🎧 Libro.fm Golden Ticket! One lucky browser will win 12 free audiobook credits.
🎡 Prize Wheel! Earn a spin with every purchase, with opportunities to win free books, merch, gift cards, and more!
📸 Photo booth!
👀 Literary Arts Bookstore & Cafe Merch Drop
Free tote bag! Be the first to rep our new merch, anyone spending $100 or more will get a free tote.
🙊 More surprises to come!

Schedule Preview:
🎈 Doors open at 9:00 a.m.
🧑‍🎨 Craft all day with collage-bookmark making supplies provided by our awesome neighbors SCRAP.
🎨 From 10:00 a.m. – 7:00 p.m. we’re very excited to have Tom Alvarado and his crew offering bookish-flash tattoos in-house! (Please note this will be first-come, first served will likely sell out. More info coming soon on designs and potential appointments.)
📖 At 11:00 a.m. we’ll be joined by local author, Leslie Barnard Booth, for a special story time.
📝 From 1:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m., preview Literary Arts programs for writers with a free pop-up Writing with Tarot workshop with Miranda Schmidt. Following the workshop Miranda will be offering free 10 minute tarot reads for creative questions for writers from 3:30-4:30.
📚→ We are honored to be among many amazing Central Eastside indie bookstores and recommend you make a day of it by visiting our friends at Mother Foucault’s, Postcard (in Cargo), and Propeller (in Urbanite).

About Independent Bookstore Day:
Independent Bookstore Day (Indie Bookstore Day, or “IBD”) was established in 2013 to promote, celebrate, and highlight the value of the Independent bookstore community. The day has been observed on the last Saturday of April every year since 2013. This year there are over 1,200 stores participating across the country.
Independent Bookstore Day is organized by the American Booksellers Association, a national not-for-profit trade organization, that works with booksellers and industry partners to ensure the success and profitability of independently owned book retailers, and to assist in expanding the community of the book.

title: FULL - Wilkes Creek Headwaters Stewardship event (NE Portland, OR)
location: 15401 NE Fremont St, Portland, OR 97230, USA
description:
====
Due to popular interest, this event is full and closed. We hope to work with you at another of our April events and/or next planting season (which starts in Oct!).
====
Celebrate Earth Week with the Greening Wilkes collective by mulching hundreds of native pollinator-friendly species at Wilkes Creek Headwaters! We may also take out some weedy introduced plants, if time allows. Note: there will be no tree-planting at this event, and this can be physically-demanding work (great for folks looking for a work out!). Our stewardship events help to ensure the highest level of plant survival through the PNW dry summer months ahead. This event will include bird walks led by the Bird Alliance of Oregon, and will end by 12pm so that people can join the Greening Wilkes celebration from 12-1:30 at nearby Wilkes Park.
The celebration will involve lunch, tabling and games from the Greening Wilkes partners- Portland Parks and Recreation, Columbia Slough Watershed Council, Verde, and The Bird Alliance of Oregon- as well as a native plant giveaway hosted by Friends of Trees! (Registration is not required to join the celebration, but it is to participate in the stewardship event.)
Please arrive by 9:45am to find our tent and sign-in, stewardship activities start promptly at 10:00am. We provide gloves, tools, and guidance. All you need to do is show up dressed for the weather and wearing sturdy shoes or boots (no sandals of any kind, please!) and be ready to have fun!
Under age 18? We request that youth 15 and under volunteer with a parent/guardian. Youth 16 and older can volunteer on their own and will need to hand us a youth waiver form signed by their parent/guardian.
Questions? Please check out our Volunteer FAQ webpage. Our team is also happy to assist! volunteer@friendsoftrees.org / 503-595-0213 We look forward to working together soon!
This event is in partnership with Portland Parks & Recreation and Portland OIC.
Funding for this event is provided by the U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service. This institution is an equal opportunity provider.

title: A Maximalist Floral Design Workshop Inspired by Marco Brambilla’s Heaven’s Gate
location: PAM CUT, 934 SW Salmon St., Portland, OR, 97205
description:
About the workshop

Morning session: 10 a.m.  – 12:30 p.m.

Afternoon session: 2 – 4:30 p.m.

Cost: $150, materials fee: $100

Ages 18+

NOTE: Registration closes on April 19, 2026.

Discover the art of storytelling through flowers in this hands-on workshop inspired by the rich visuals and layered opulence of Marco Brambilla’s video collage Heaven’s Gate. We’ll explore how flowers can convey drama, excess, and narrative, transforming seasonal blooms into bold, immersive arrangements.

The workshop begins with a guided gallery walk to see the artwork Heaven’s Gate to spark inspiration, followed by an immersive floral session where you’ll receive all the tools, tips, and a curated selection of vibrant, seasonal flowers to create your own elegant, maximalist floral still life. No experience is required—just bring your love of flowers, art, and imagination.

Led by Portland-based floral artist Bianca Sparta of Colibri, celebrated for her eclectic and extravagant designs, this workshop welcomes every approach—from soft and subtle to daringly dramatic. Together, we’ll respond to the textures, colors, and stories in Brambilla’s artwork to craft arrangements that are as layered, grandiose, and captivating as his cinematic world.

register for morning session

register for afternoon session

About the teaching artist

Colibri is Bianca Sparta. With over a decade of experience working with flowers, Bianca brings her fine art background to intersect with modern day florals, creating a unique aesthetic and retail environment that stands alone.

title: Bonsai Society of Portland Exhibition
location: Portland Japanese Garden, 611 SW Kingston Ave, Portland, OR, 97205, United States
description: Portland Japanese Garden welcomes the Bonsai Society of Portland (BSOP) for a bonsai exhibition in the both the Yanai Family Classroom, located in the Jordan Schnitzer Japanese Arts Learning Center, and the Lemelson Studio. Bonsai, which literally translates to “tree-in-a-tray,” is the art and science of miniature trees. Literal translation aside, “bonsai” has evolved to mean an artistically shaped woody plant that is intended to suggest the image of a mature tree in nature. The creation of a miniaturized landscape fulfills the human yearning for a connection to nature in the smallest of spaces. This exhibition will include dozens of bonsai from BSOP members’ private collections, including several world-class examples of this ancient Japanese art form. Guests will see coniferous, deciduous, fruiting, and flowering species, ranging in size from three-foot-tall specimens to tiny shohin trees small enough to hold in the palm of your hand. Shohin will be on display in the Lemelson Studio. Included with garden admission.

title: EPISTOLARY POEMS
location: Literary Arts
description:
While letters are kept private, our poems, however intimate, are often intended for public audiences. The epistolary poem is a marriage of these disparate domains. Participants in this one day class will read, draft, and collaborate in revising letter poems that balance the public with the private, the close-to-bone with the common. What’s shared will buoy what’s unsaid; our poems will be meditations on this tension. Through generative, constraint-based prompts, participants will explore the tension between forms of direct address and forms of poetic allusion to speak to, or point towards, what’s been left unsaid in their poems.

title: Chef Demo: Peter Cho - Han Oak
location: STEELPORT Knife Co. 3602 Northeast Sandy Boulevard #Suite B Portland, OR 97232 Born in Korea and raised in Oregon, Peter Cho has become a defining voice in Portland’s food scene. After graduating from the University of Oregon, he spent 12 years in New York City working his way up to executive chef and director within a Michelin-starred restaurant group. In 2016, Cho and his wife, Sun Young Park, returned to Oregon and opened Han Oak, their Korean-American restaurant set inside their home, followed by Toki in 2021. In 2023, they opened Jeju, a wood-fired Korean barbecue restaurant centered on whole-animal butchery and locally sourced, sustainably raised ingredients. Across his restaurants, Cho blends tradition with innovation while fostering mentorship and learning for emerging chefs. We’re excited to welcome Peter to STEELPORT, where he’ll demonstrate the knife skills central to Korean cuisine and prepare samples of a dish for everyone to enjoy. RSVP below for a chance to win

title: Garden Tea Tastings with Hannah Ma (11 AM)
location: Lan Su Chinese Garden, 239 NW Everett Street, Portland, Oregon, 97209
description:
Overview

Tickets

Tea Master

Series Overview

This spring, take a front-row seat to Chinese tea culture with our intimate Garden Tea Tasting Series (March–May), led by tea master Hannah Ma. Savor three seasonal teas from Yun Shui Teahouse, learn traditional brewing techniques, and explore the stories behind centuries of tea culture. Your ticket includes admission to Lan Su Chinese Garden on the day of your tasting.

After your 1-hour tasting, you’ll receive a porcelain teacup to continue your journey at home. All sampled teas will also be available for purchase in our Yun Shui Teahouse.

Full Series Schedule

Saturdays & Sundays, March 21–April 26 | 11:00 AM & 1:00 PM

Fridays & Sundays, May 1–May 31 | 1:00 PM & 3:00 PM

Get Tickets

Seating is very limited for these intimate group tastings, so reserve your seat early. Your ticket includes garden admission on the day of your tasting.

Lan Su Members & Guests: $36.95

Non-Members: $55.95

Note: A $0.95 service fee is reflected in each paid ticket

Meet the Tea Master: Hannah Ma

A Portland native, Hannah grew up drinking tea almost as often as water. Her passion was formally cultivated during her senior year of high school, when she gained extensive experience with diverse tea blends and preparation techniques as a tea-rista at Portal Tea Company (formerly Tea Chai Té). Now a beverage enthusiast of more than six years, Hannah is thrilled to join Lan Su’s Tea Tasting program, where she shares science-based insights into tea’s properties and explores the rich traditions of Chinese-style tea ceremonies.

Free Lan Su Parking

There is free first come, first served parking in our sister lot next to the garden at 424 NW Third Avenue. Additional metered parking and garages are available on surrounding streets.

title: Fire Ceremony and Purification, Meditation: Drop-In
location: Ananda Temple in Beaverton, 4855 SW Watson Avenue, Beaverton, Oregon, 97005, United States
description:
A Vedic Fire Ceremony and Purification Ceremony is open to all on Sunday mornings at 9:00 am, followed by meditation. This is offered in the sanctuary, prior to Sunday Service, which begins at 10 am.

Details of these ceremonies can be found HERE.

Two mantras are repeated seven times, while ghee and rice are added to the fire. The ghee represents our heart's devotion and the grains of rice represent our karma that keeps us from perfect union with God. The fire is the divine light that is the source of all that is. We repeat the mantras with a recording of Swami Kriyananda chanting in Sanskrit.

The fire ceremony is followed by a Purification Ceremony and silent meditation which ends at 9:45.

All are welcome.
Gayatri Mantra
Om
Bhur bhuvah swah;
Om tat savitur varenyam
bhargo devasya dhimahi
dhiyo yo nah prachodayat.
Om
Translation:
We meditate on the Supreme Effulgence
of the three universes.
May It enlighten our consciousness.

The Mahamritunjaya Mantra
Om
Triambakam yajamahe
sugandim pushti vardhanam
urvarukam eva bhandhan
mrityor mukshiya mamritat
Swaha.
Translation:
We worship that One of divine vision
who nourishes all living beings.
May He free us from death
and grant us immortality.

title: Bonsai Society of Portland Exhibition
location: Portland Japanese Garden, 611 SW Kingston Ave, Portland, OR, 97205, United States
description: Portland Japanese Garden welcomes the Bonsai Society of Portland (BSOP) for a bonsai exhibition in the both the Yanai Family Classroom, located in the Jordan Schnitzer Japanese Arts Learning Center, and the Lemelson Studio. Bonsai, which literally translates to “tree-in-a-tray,” is the art and science of miniature trees. Literal translation aside, “bonsai” has evolved to mean an artistically shaped woody plant that is intended to suggest the image of a mature tree in nature. The creation of a miniaturized landscape fulfills the human yearning for a connection to nature in the smallest of spaces. This exhibition will include dozens of bonsai from BSOP members’ private collections, including several world-class examples of this ancient Japanese art form. Guests will see coniferous, deciduous, fruiting, and flowering species, ranging in size from three-foot-tall specimens to tiny shohin trees small enough to hold in the palm of your hand. Shohin will be on display in the Lemelson Studio. Included with garden admission.

title: Bring Your Story to the Stage
location: Literary Arts
description:
This class is for anyone ready to take a personal 5-minute story and actively shape it for an audience. You’ll work hands-on with one story. Drafting, refining, and testing it aloud. We’ll focus on structure, pacing, and point of view, helping you find the spine of the story and decide what belongs in this particular version of the story and what doesn’t. You’ll practice starting strong, building momentum, and landing the story with intention.
Taught by BACKFENCE Storytelling producers and hosts Frayn Masters and Ash Allen, this class is ideal if you’ve taken Small Stories, Big Meaning or already have a personal story you’re curious to bring forward—whether for a stage, or simply to hear it land out loud.
Rather than “performing,” this class emphasizes shaping a vulnerable narrative. You’ll receive demonstrations and feedback on mic use, voice, presence, and timing in a supportive room, with clear guidance.
By the end of the workshop, you’ll have:
•	A shaped draft you can continue developing
•	Practical tools for revising and rehearsing
•	Greater confidence telling a personal story aloud
•	A clearer sense of how you want to show up onstage
You set the pace. Participation is encouraged but never forced. The goal is clarity, connection, and momentum—not polish or performance.

Series Overview

This spring, take a front-row seat to Chinese tea culture with our intimate Garden Tea Tasting Series (March–May), led by tea master Hannah Ma. Savor three seasonal teas from Yun Shui Teahouse, learn traditional brewing techniques, and explore the stories behind centuries of tea culture. Meet the Tea Master: Hannah Ma

A Portland native, Hannah grew up drinking tea almost as often as water. Her passion was formally cultivated during her senior year of high school, when she gained extensive experience with diverse tea blends and preparation techniques as a tea-rista at Portal Tea Company (formerly Tea Chai Té). Now a beverage enthusiast of more than six years, Hannah is thrilled to join Lan Su’s Tea Tasting program, where she shares science-based insights into tea’s properties and explores the rich traditions of Chinese-style tea ceremonies.

title: Celebrate Spring! — Finley Wildlife Refuge + Picnic Lunch
location: Finley Wildlife Refuge
description:
Join the South Willamette Valley alumni chapter at Finley National Wildlife Refuge—walking, birding, and having a picnic in celebration of spring!

The refuge is located approximately 10 miles south of Corvallis west of Highway 99W. It protects and manages over 50,000 acres of native Willamette Valley wet prairie and oak savannah. It supports thousands of species and is known for fantastic birding and hiking. It preserves what the Willamette Valley might have looked like when the Kalapuya, indigenous Native American peoples of the Willamette Valley, used fire to manage the valley's prairies for thousands of years. The refuge uses a variety of management practices to preserve these rare habitats.

Things to pack: a picnic lunch, weather appropriate clothing, binoculars, and sketching or art supplies. We will have a mindful scavenger hunt, some watercolor supplies to share, and dessert for everyone. This is a rain or shine event. There is a covered pavilion with benches; camp chairs are also a good idea. Kids and friends are welcome to join!

Don’t forget to RSVP here. If you’re attending, watch for an email from Ashley before the event with location/meeting point details. The address listed is not our meeting place. It is the address of the refuge offices. We will provide directions to meeting place in a group reminder to those who RSVP.

Hosted by Amanda ‘91, Ashley ‘07, and Jewel ‘82

title: Garden Tea Tastings with Hannah Ma (1 PM)
location: Lan Su Chinese Garden, 239 NW Everett Street, Portland, Oregon, 97209
description:
Overview

Tickets

Tea Master

Parking & Directions

Series Overview

This spring, take a front-row seat to Chinese tea culture with our intimate Garden Tea Tasting Series (March–May), led by tea master Hannah Ma. Savor three seasonal teas from Yun Shui Teahouse, learn traditional brewing techniques, and explore the stories behind centuries of tea culture. Your ticket includes admission to Lan Su Chinese Garden on the day of your tasting.

After your 1-hour tasting, you’ll receive a porcelain teacup to continue your journey at home. All sampled teas will also be available for purchase in our Yun Shui Teahouse.

Full Series Schedule

Saturdays & Sundays, March 21–April 26 | 11:00 AM & 1:00 PM

Fridays & Sundays, May 1–May 31 | 1:00 PM & 3:00 PM

Get Tickets

Seating is very limited for these intimate group tastings, so reserve your seat early. Your ticket includes garden admission on the day of your tasting.

Lan Su Members & Guests: $36.95

Non-Members: $55.95

Note: A $0.95 service fee is reflected in each paid ticket

Meet the Tea Master: Hannah Ma

A Portland native, Hannah grew up drinking tea almost as often as water. Her passion was formally cultivated during her senior year of high school, when she gained extensive experience with diverse tea blends and preparation techniques as a tea-rista at Portal Tea Company (formerly Tea Chai Té). Now a beverage enthusiast of more than six years, Hannah is thrilled to join Lan Su’s Tea Tasting program, where she shares science-based insights into tea’s properties and explores the rich traditions of Chinese-style tea ceremonies.

Parking & Directions

Free Lan Su Parking

There is free first come, first served parking in our sister lot next to the garden at 424 NW Third Avenue. Additional metered parking and garages are available on surrounding streets.

description:
Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

Portland Code & Coffee
\#\# What to Expect:

At Beaverton Code and Coffee, we currently have informal hosting with multiple rotating hosts. If you are a regular attendee (2+ times/month), feel free to ask more about it, and I can add you as co-host!

Code and Coffee is an inclusive, informal co-working session. Drink some coffee, bring your laptop, and have engaging conversations. This is a great opportunity to learn from others, share your knowledge, and possibly collaborate on side projects, online courses, or even your day-to-day work tasks.

Still uncertain? Let's chat on Discord! [https://discord.gg/JbGyY3bKTS](https://discord.gg/JbGyY3bKTS)

title: Forest Bathing
location: Hoyt Arboretum, 4000 SW Fairview Blvd, Portland, OR, 97221, United States
description: Experience a guided forest bathing walk through Hoyt Arboretum’s unique tree collection and forested areas. Forest Bathing offers many health benefits from stress relief to immune system and mood support. Forest therapy is a research-based framework for supporting healing and wellness through immersion in forests and other natural environments. Forest therapy is inspired by the Japanese practice of Shinrin-Yoku, which translates to “forest bathing.” Studies have demonstrated a wide array of health benefits, especially in the cardiovascular and immune systems, and for stabilizing and improving mood and cognition. We build on those benefits and look beyond, to what happens when people remember that we are a part of nature, not separate from it, and are related to all other beings in fundamental ways. This event is coordinated by Hoyt Arboretum and registration is required through their website.

title: Rerouted: How the Making (and unmaking) of Shipping Lines defines our World
location: Psychology, 105
description:
The story of global trade and shipping is often narrated as one of ever-increasing efficiency and speed, of transitions from sail to steam to cargo and futures of automation—of making straight lines. But, for as long as there has been trade (and ships) there have been delays and interruptions—rerouters and rerouting. I argue that disruptions and moments when things appear to be stuck or rerouted are neither aberrations nor failures. Rerouting, far from being an exception, is both the norm and, at times, such as this contemporary moment of trade wars and resurgent forms of violence, the condition desired by many as a mode of profit and possibility.

To showcase the productive possibilities of rerouting, I focus on one sea route—the Bab-el- Mandeb, a key chokepoint for global trade connecting Europe to Asia and the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean. In 2023, in response to Houthi attacks on merchant ships, this shipping route briefly disappeared, as cargo ships were rerouted through the Cape of Good Hope. I tell this story of this rerouting and its consequences both ephemeral and long-lasting from the perspective of a mobile set of actors in the Red Sea. Locating them within longer histories and wider geographies, I argue for the centrality of interruptions within our understandings of circulation and crossings in the Indian Ocean and beyond.

Jatin Dua is an associate professor of Anthropology at the University of Michigan. He also directs the Oceans Lab at the University of Michigan dedicated to collaborative and multimodal ways of engaging oceans as anthropological interlocutors. His research explores maritime mobility, and its perils and possibilities, in the Indian Ocean, focusing on processes and projects of governance, law, and economy. His book, Captured at Sea: Piracy and Protection in the Indian Ocean, published with the University of California Press (December 2019) [winner of the 2020 Elliot P. Skinner Book Award; shortlisted for the 2024 Monsoon Book Prize and translated into Italian and Greek] is a multi-sited ethnographic and archival engagement with Somali piracy and contestations over legitimate and illegitimate commerce in the Western Indian Ocean. In addition, he has published several articles on maritime anthropology, captivity, political economy, and sovereignty in Public Culture, American Ethnologist, Cultural Anthropology, Ethnos, Annual Review of Anthropology, History and Anthropology and Comparative Studies in Society and History. He is currently the editor-in-chief of Comparative Studies in Society and History.

description:

Decompress and connect at the end of your work week with meditation practice and community. This event is in partnership with the Young Meditators Group of Portland.

**No experience required, and meditators of all traditions are welcome.**
**Cushions will be provided but feel free to bring your own.**

**SCHEDULE**

**6:30 – 7:00PM Silent Meditation**
Silent meditation practice (you are welcome to practice a silent meditation of your choosing)

**7:00 – 7:25PM Meditative Talking Circle**
Resting on the foundation of meditation practice, this talking circle practice expands to include others in the circle. While maintaining a meditation practice, members of the circle are welcome to speak from the present moment, though speaking is not required to participate. Instructions will be provided at the beginning so please arrive on time for this part of the practice.

**7:25PM Closing and Social**
There will be some time after group to connect after practice, after which the group may choose to go out for drinks and snacks at a nearby pub within walking distance.

This is a 'by donation' event. Suggested donation amount $3-10: [Please Donate Here](https://www.paypal.com/donate?hosted_button_id=PPCNJX8KYKY42)

title: Priscilla Bernard Wieden in conversation with Kim Stafford
location: Literary Arts
description:
The Literary Arts Bookstore and Cafe is excited to welcome Literary Arts board member Priscilla Bernard Wieden for a special reading from her poetry collection, Solitary Light. Priscilla will be in conversation with Oregon’s former poet laureate, Kim Stafford.

About the book:

Poetry is a conduit for communicating our shared experiences and broadening our understanding of ourselves and each other. In her debut book of poetry, Solitary Light, Priscilla Bernard Wieden shares her journey when the unspeakable happens, and then offers every grieving widow a glimmer of light. These poems are a beacon to help you find your way out of the despair of grief, to help you look deep inside your own spirit, and emerge with a heart full of loving memories as you find the beauty in joyful living that still awaits you.

title: Weekly Forest Park Tuesday Hike and Pizza (Lower Macleay to Pittock Mansion)
description:
Portland, Outdoors (20s and 30s Hiking Group)
A weekly hike up to Pittock Mansion to view the city!

Miles: 5.0
Elevation Gain: 921 ft

Things to bring: headlamp/flashlight during the short days of winter (it gets dark on this hike starting in September!), hiking boots, water.

Please note that although this hike is relatively short, the elevation gain in such a short period can be challenging for those that are beginning to hike. The group maintains a steady, constant pace on the trail and if you cannot keep up, keep hiking and we will wait at the top for you!

This hike is in the heavy woods of Forest Park and gets darker much earlier that the surrounding areas due to this tree coverage. We hike all year round and will shorten the hike during very rainy days in the winter to a 2.5-mile round trip hike.

Alltrails link: Lower Macleay Park to Pittock Mansion on AllTrails
https://www.alltrails.com/trail/us/oregon/lower-macleay-park-to-pittock-mansion?p=-1&sh=duboim

title: Writer's Group: Workshop - Unlock Your Writing: Using Tarot to Deepen the Creative Process
location: Garden Home Community Library, This is a virtual meeting. Details will be emailed to registrants.
description:
This is a virtual meeting. Registrants will receive all details.
Unlock Your Writing: Using Tarot to Deepen the Creative Process with Meg Hayertz
Whether you have a deep relationship with the Tarot, or have never pulled a card, this workshop offers simple techniques for reading ourselves, our blocks, and the messages in our creative works. When we stop succumbing to our challenges or bulldozing through them, and instead listen to our creative blocks, we find inspiration, motivation, and momentum in our creative practice. What would it be like to draft, revise, and complete a project without losing connection with yourself or with the energy that guides you? Come find out! In this workshop, you will gain insight and momentum around a creative challenge or block. All genres and skill levels welcome. Tarot cards will be provided.
About our presenter:
Meg Hayertz
(she/they) is the author of
Tarot for Beginners
(Althea Press) and the founder of Creative Momentum, where she helps writers free their voice, nourish their practice, and finish their project. She holds an MFA from California Institute of Integral Studies and her fiction has appeared in
The Louisville Review
,
CALYX
,
Press Pause, VoiceCatcher
, and elsewhere. She lives in Portland, Oregon with her partner and cat. Visit her at
www.CreativeMomentum.art
and on YouTube
@MakeItMeanIt

title: Devotion:  Yoga in Daily Life FREE class
location: Ananda Portland Temple, 4855 SW Watson Ave, Beaverton, OR, 97005, United States
description:
“A single spark may start a forest fire. The smallest step toward God can be a beginning in the process of soul-awakening. The Bhagavad Gita says, “To him who offers Me even a flower or a leaf with devotion, I Myself come and receive his offering.” The smallest expression of pure love can be the spark that ignites a fire of devotion which ultimately consumes the forest of our desires and leaves our consciousness free to soar untrammeled in infinite skies.”

— Swami Kriyananda, The Promise of Immortality
What is devotion? How do we cultivate it in our hearts and minds so the path to God is not littered with the debris of delusion?

Let's dive into devotion and explore how, when, why, and where devotion fits into our lives.

Led by Lorna

Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: Mid-day Break Concert with David Rothman
description:
Concert pianist David Rothman performs 8 Noveletten, Opus 21 and Piano Concerto in A major by Robert Schumann, with Michael Barnes, organ as orchestra.

Pianist David Rothman has delighted TOC audiences with performances of the entire Schubert Cycle, Mozart Cycle, and all of Chopin’s solo piano pieces. With Michael Barnes on the organ, Rothman has also played the Rachmaninoff Third and Brahms Second Piano Concerto at TOC. As a child, Rothman attended the Yehudi Menuhin School, then the Curtis Institute of Music.

Michael Barnes is a professional pianist and organist, and has been Senior Organist at Westminster since 1992. With the Westminster Presbyterian Church Chancel Choir, he has toured Scotland and Cuba. He has performed with the Wednesday Noon Concert Series at The Old Church Concert Hall since 1988. With the Portland Gay Men's Chorus, he toured China for goodwill concerts in 2019. He accompanies the Pacific Youth Choir, and is Organist at Westminster Presbyterian Church and Temple Beth Israel in Portland, OR. He is a member of the American Guild of Organists, Organ Historical Society and Guild of Temple Musicians.

title: Truth or Fiction? Verifying AI-Generated Answers
location: Virtual
description:
Generative artificial intelligence tools like ChatGPT can produce convincing answers, but not all of them are based on reliable sources. In this hands-on workshop, you’ll learn how to write balanced prompts to reduce bias in text generated by common AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, and how to fact-check those responses using proven information literacy strategies. This session will demonstrate practical skills to use AI chatbots responsibly and verify the accuracy of the text they generate.

After the session, learners will be able to:

Craft effective prompts for use with public generative AI chatbots such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, etc.
Describe the strengths and limitations of generative AI for information search and retrieval
Use information literacy skills and tools to evaluate AI-generated text output

This workshop will be recorded, and the recording will be shared with all registered attendees after the session. If you cannot make the workshop date and time, you are welcome to register in order to receive a copy of the recording.

title: Denim Day
location: Gray Campus Center, Patio
description:
Denim Day is a campaign on a Wednesday in April where folks wear denim to demonstrate support for survivors and challenge myths supporting sexual violence. The campaign began after a ruling by the Italian Supreme Court in 1999, where a rape conviction was overturned after the judges ruled that the jeans worn by the victim were too tight to not have been removed by the victim–thereby implying consent. The day following the ruling, women in the Italian Parliament came to work wearing jeans in solidarity with the victim.

Come by our table outside the GCC to add your patch to our Denim Quilt and show your allied support for survivors.

title: Documentary Screening: Silent War, Asian American Reckonings with Mental Health
location: Corbett House, Living Room 112
description: The AAPI ERG is hosting a screening of Silent War from 5:00–7:00 p.m. in Corbett House Living Room 112. While all identities are welcome and encouraged to participate, the focus of social will focus on supporting Asian, Asian American, and Pacific Islander identifying communities.Documentary Synopsis:Silent War: Asian American Reckonings with Mental Health is a groundbreaking documentary that confronts the deep silence surrounding mental illness in Asian American communities. Through intimate stories of struggle, survival, and healing, the film explores how cultural stigma, intergenerational trauma, racism, and systemic neglect have shaped the mental health experiences of families from diverse Asian backgrounds. Featuring raw personal testimonies, expert insights, and emotional family reckonings, Silent War reveals the human cost of staying silent—and the power of breaking that silence. At once personal and political, the film charts a collective journey from shame to resilience, offering hope for a more inclusive and compassionate mental health future.  If you have questions, please direct them to Dr. Amy Wang, amycwang@lclark.edu (mailto:amycwang@lclark.edu).

title: Run & Chug!
description:
Portland Fun Run
The route will be posted soon! In the meantime, here are some FAQs:

**Where do I find the group?**
We typically meet up right outside the bar! We rotate through a variety of bars and breweries. Check out our past events to see what places we typically go to.

**What is the average pace of the group?**
There is a wide range of paces that varies week-to-week, but typically most people are between 7:30 - 10 minute miles. We welcome all runners, regardless of pace (the #1 goal our group is to make new friends, not break records), but we advise making sure you are comfortable with the route if you are worried you might be slower than this range, just so you don’t get lost.

* Need a running buddy or want to check if anyone else in the group is running your pace? Feel free to message Erin to coordinate this! Please send any messages by Tuesday evening the day before we meet 😊

**What time does the group actually start running?**
We suggest runners arrive around 6:55pm, but we do not actually start running until 7:05pm.

**When is the route posted?**
The route is posted typically Tuesday night or Wednesday morning.
I don’t have a car, what do I do with my belongings while I’m running?
One option is to wear a running belt to keep keys, ID, credit card, etc. on you while you run, but if you show up a little early, you can often find someone who is willing to put your jacket or other belongings in their car for you during the run.

**What should I bring?**
Make sure to bring your ID and credit card/cash for the bar. Additionally, in the winter, we recommend bringing a light to run with and wearing something reflective. Lastly, we are sometimes outside for drinks, depending on the location, so it’s a good idea to bring a jacket.

title: Morning Group Meditation
location: Ananda Temple in Beaverton, 4855 SW Watson Avenue, Beaverton, Oregon, 97005, United States
description:
Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: Watson Fellowship Webinar
description:
Curious about what it’s like to spend a year pursuing an independent project around the world?

Join Watson Foundation staff and Watson Fellows on Thursday, April 30 from noon–1 p.m. pacific time for the Spring Watson Webinar to explore the incredible opportunity offered by the Thomas J. Watson Fellowship!

Staff and fellows will share insights into the program and the application process in this national webinar.

Featured Watson Fellows:

Julia Thomas, 2017 Fellow. “Community Voices: Exploring the Intersections of Storytelling, Citizenship and Journalism”Tommy Shenoi, 2024 Fellow. “Cultivating Transformative Resilience with Global Mycology”About the Fellowship:

The mission of the Thomas J. Watson Fellowship Program is to offer recent college graduates of unusual promise a year of purposeful, independent exploration and travel outside of the United States. Fellows conceive original projects and embrace the ensuing journey. They decide where to go, who to meet and when to change course. They receive a stipend of $40,000 to support them in these endeavors. During the year, fellows enhance their capacity for resourcefulness, imagination, openness, and leadership and foster their humane and effective participation in the world community.

🌍 Curious? Inspired? Wondering if this could be your next step?

Current First Years, Sophomores, Juniors, and spring/fall Seniors are all welcome to attend, as well as international students. The 2027 application opens on April 30, 2026, for students graduating next academic year.

Register for the Zoom webinar at the link in this event.

title: ENVS Spring Poster Celebration
location: Stamm
description: Please join us in celebrating the end of the semester and the work that students have conducted in their ENVS and CORE courses this semester! The following classes will be represented in the poster celebration:ENVS 295 Environmental Engagement: Students will present public communication materials they created using data collected during community mapping engagement methods in two Portland city parks - Gabriel Park and Irving Park. The materials will both speak to engagement participant's perspective and experience with open and public space planning, and inform the public on how to engage with this topic further in Portland.   ENVS 350 Environmental Theory: Students will present posters summarizing their environmental praxis projects, grounding a key theory concept in the real world.  ENVS 400 Senior Seminar: Students will present individual posters on their capstone projects.  ENVS 400 Senior Seminar (North Portland capstone section): Students will present outcomes of their Albina-based senior environmental research, via individual posters and team-based StoryMaps and a new website, us (http://albinamaps.us/).  ENVS 490 Landscape Mapping and Monitoring: Students will present their landscape mapping and monitoring results from semester long investigations in land use and land cover changes.  CORE 121 Measuring Environmental Meaning: Students will present posters summarizing the results of their original team-based environmental surveys.  CORE 121 Take Charge! Tackling Environmental Problems: Students will present posters summarizing their whole-class proposals for improving transportation at LC.    This event will be held in Stamm, in Fowler Student Center. Snacks will be provided.

title: Faulkner and Morrison: Absalom, Absalom! and Beloved
location: Literary Arts
description:
In this Delve, we’ll read William Faulkner’s Absalom, Absalom! (1936) and Toni Morrison’s Beloved (1987), both of which consider the many scars, healed and not, caused by enslavement and the Civil War. Thinking about history, memory, and what Morrison calls “rememory,” we’ll consider what it means to live in a nation, to inherit its past, and to fight for a better future.
There are many excellent reasons to read William Faulkner and Toni Morrison in tandem. Morrison herself articulates a crucial one in a 1981 interview, where she aligns her aims as a writer with what Faulkner’s fiction accomplished: “[He] wrote what I suppose could be called regional literature and had it published all over the world. It is good—and universal—because it is specifically about a particular world. That’s what I wish to do.” It doesn’t matter that Yoknapatawpha County only exists on the map that Faulkner sketches, his novels bring it to vivid and complicated life. Morrison’s fiction does something similar for her characters, usually Black women who she depicts with caring attention and particularity. Without ever erasing what is unique about their experiences, she makes sure that persons long overlooked can be seen by readers around the world as “good—and universal.”
A compelling case can be make that one of these two authors is the “best” U.S. writer of the twentieth century. Their works are formally innovative and unflinching in their assessment of the nation’s history, particularly as it concerns enslavement and its long aftermaths. Here, too, Morrison offers a crucial key to what reading this “American” past can mean when done with deft care: “The most valuable point of entry into the question of cultural (or racial) distinction, the one most fraught, is its language—its unpoliced, seditious, confrontational, manipulative, inventive, disruptive, masked, and unmasking language.” She may be talking about reading nineteenth-century fiction in the passage but it also offers an excellent guide for thinking about the kind of work she (and Faulkner) wrote, especially as they pressure words to try and account for “unspeakable things unspoken.”
Texts:
Absalom, Absalom by William Faulkner
Beloved by Toni Morrison
