title: Mindfulness Tour
location: Portland Japanese Garden, 611 SW Kingston Ave., Portland, OR, 97205, United States
description:
Portland Japanese Garden members touring the Sand and Stone Garden. Photo by Peter Friedman.

This intimate tour focuses not on meditation, but instead on learning to bring mindful awareness to oneself, and the world around us, through intentional observation and connections.

An experienced guide will provide a foundation for the art of contemplative exploration throughout various Garden spaces, and gently guide awareness away from the busyness of everyday life, back toward the connection to nature and experience of peace.

Each tour will be slightly unique to focus on the current season, weather (occurs rain or shine), and garden spaces. However, these tours are designed and intended to help members continue to enhance future Garden visits through independent mindful practice through all seasons.

Tours will begin in the Atsuhiko and Ina Goodwin Tateuchi Foundation Courtyard starting at 9:00am, and typically last about 45-60 minutes.

Space limited to 10 members. Reservations are required and restricted to a maximum of two per person regardless of membership level.

title: In Divine Friendship: A Zoom Book Study
description:
What is Divine Friendship?

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have, such as:

Strengthening one's faith
Acceleration of spiritual progress
Standing up for truth
Meditating more deeply
Responding to illness
Earning a living
Attracting a mate
Raising children
Overcoming negative self-judgments
Responding to world upheavals

Connecting all of these letters is the love, compassion, and wisdom of Swami Kriyananda, one of the leading spiritual figures of our times.

The letters describe in detail his efforts to fulfill his Guru's commission to establish spiritual communities—"would brotherhood colonies"—and offer invaluable advice to leaders everywhere on how to avoid the temptations of materialism, selfishness, and pride. A spiritual treasure that speaks to spiritual seekers at all levels.

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have

Join Surendra and friends near and far in this fascinating discussion about Yogananda's teachings on the changing consciousness of humankind across the ages.

Surendra is a member of Ananda Portland's ministry team, and has studied and lived the teachings of Yogananda while serving Ananda in Seattle, Palo Alto, India and Portland. He is also an author of 5 books of spiritual essays and poetry.

 

Register for this weekly book study below. The length of the course depends entirely on the pace set by the group. We invite you to pay a one-time fee for the course on a sliding scale.

After you register, you will be sent the Zoom link to attend the weekly discussions.

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

title: Visual Journals in the Classroom (In-Person)
location: Lewis & Clark College, TBA
description: This course will introduce visual journals as an instrument for generating ideas and documenting the creative process.  Participants will have the opportunity to begin their own visual journal. They will participate in several art-making activities over the course of five days, using a variety of media that encourage the artist to develop creative routines and/or processes.  These activities are meant to encourage the artist to develop unique ideas and cultivate an individual point of view. Over time, the creative choices and chances that accumulate in the visual journal act as both evidence of and a resource for unique and inspiring ideas. We will discuss how the visual journal essentially acts as a teaching assistant in the curriculum to support/level content for students at a variety of ability levels.  This course will focus mainly on the way the visual journal can support creative thinking in artistic applications, but some attention will be given to writing, text and strategies for making ideas more visual.Details & RegistrationDates: Wednesdays-Thursdays, June 17-18, Monday-Wednesday, June 22-24, 2026, 9 a.m.-3 p.m.Location: Lewis & Clark College, TBAGraduate Continuing Education Credit: CEED-849-21, 2 semester hours, $770Register Online (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/4735371)We are committed to making our events accessible to all needs and abilities. Please be aware that the process for evaluation and implementation of accommodations could take 2-3 weeks, so please be in touch with the OSA as soon as possible. Email access@lclark.edu (mailto:access@lclark.edu) with any additional questions or concerns.About the InstructorMichael Dodson has taught art at French Prairie Middle School for 27 years. He has led workshops and sessions on using visual journals in the classroom at state and national educator conferences. Praised for her “brilliant coloratura voice,” “world class” stage presence, and ability to “elicit beautiful passages with ease” Madeline Ross has forged a path in the music industry as a performer, collaborator, and educator. She is an award-winning and sought-after performing artist as an opera, concert, musical theater, and jazz vocalist; she serves as the Executive Director of Renegade Opera, Portland’s unconventional opera company; and she teaches voice at Reed College.

Ms. Ross is known for her “supreme performance” of Ligeti’s Mysteries of the Macabre that is “simultaneously intense, dramatic, and humorous” and was a National Finalist of the NATS Artist Awards in 2024. She was hailed for “effortlessly nailing” her performance as Queen of the Night in Mozart’s Die Zauberflöte. Recent performances include Witchfinder, Waking the Witch (Day) with Renegade Opera, Lucinda, Dark Sisters (Muhly) with Eugene Opera, First Woodsprite Rusalka (Dvorak) with Portland Opera, and Daughter in the world premiere of Qaqnus (Sahba Aminikia) with Music of Remembrance (Seattle).

Ms. Ross made her Carnegie Hall debut in 2019 as a jazz soloist where she “scatt[ed] to beat the band” (NY Concert Review). To see upcoming performances visit her website.

description:
Photo Courtesy of Oregon Koto Kai

Enjoy a free koto performance by Oregon Koto-Kai at 1:15pm at the Cathy Rudd Cultural Corner in the Jordan Schnitzer Japanese Arts Learning Center.

About the Koto

The standard Koto is a thirteen-string plucked zither introduced to Japan in the 7th century. It has been part of the Gagaku court ensemble for over a thousand years, becoming popular among the merchant classes in the Edo period (1600-1868). An important member of the traditional Sankyoku ensemble, along with the three-string Shamisen and Shakuhachi (bamboo flute), the Koto developed further in a solo capacity, eventually becoming one of Japan’s most prominent musical instruments. Today, its varied repertoire and wide range of playing techniques provide a rich palette of sound textures, making the Koto appealing to audiences worldwide. Learn more about Koto.

Oregon Koto-Kai

Oregon Koto-Kai is a group passionate about the Japanese koto, a 13-stringed zither with over 1000 years of history. Founded by Mitsuki Dazai in February 2012, the ensemble performed its first concert in Portland, Oregon. Since then, they have performed throughout the state at venues like the Portland Japanese Garden, Portland Rose Festival, and Oregon Shakespeare Festival in Ashland. Their mission is to introduce Japanese koto music to the broader community by providing concerts and lessons. Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: Trauma-Informed Breathwork for Nervous System Regulation in Clinical Practice (Online)
location: Online
description: This experiential workshop introduces clinicians to trauma-informed breathwork as a practical, ethical, and accessible tool for nervous system regulation in clinical settings.  Grounded in somatic psychology, polyvagal-informed approaches, and breath-based interventions, this training provides clinicians with concrete techniques they can immediately integrate into their work with clients experiencing anxiety, trauma-related stress, and nervous system dysregulation.  The workshop is organized around a four-phase somatic arc—Root, Release, Integrate, and Embody—which offers clinicians a structured framework for understanding how breathwork and somatic interventions can be applied at different stages of trauma recovery.  Participants will learn how to use breathwork for stabilization and resourcing, how to safely support emotional and somatic release, and how to facilitate integration through gentle parts-based and inner child–informed practices.  In clinical settings, this training emphasizes integration before embodiment, ensuring safety, pacing, and nervous system stabilization. This sequencing helps clinicians develop a clear understanding of when and how to use breath-based interventions in an ethical, trauma-informed, culturally responsive, and clinically sound manner.Following this workshop, participants will be able to:Describe how trauma impacts the nervous system and breathing patterns.  Explain the four phases of somatic trauma recovery: Root, Release, Integrate, and Embody.  Demonstrate at least three trauma-informed breathwork techniques for nervous system regulation.Identify appropriate breath-based interventions based on a client's window of tolerance and readiness.  Integrate breathwork and somatic awareness into existing clinical models.  Details & RegistrationDate: Thursday, June 18, 2026, 1-5 p.m. PT, OnlineInstructor: Caroline McGrath, LPC, NCCDetails: $105, includes 4 CEUs. Alumni and Adjuncts save 20%. $45 GSEC Student Rate.Register Online (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/wf1W4MQ?epid=a1aUY000002ULDx)  Limited no-cost registrations for GSEC Clinical Mental Health Supervisors, Faculty, and Staff. Email cce@lclark.edu (mailto:cce@lclark.edu).Registration closes after Monday, June 15thAccessibility: We are committed to making our events accessible to all needs and abilities. When registering, please let us know your access needs. Contact us at 503-768-6040 or cce@lclark.edu (mailto:cce@lclark.edu) with questions.Please note: Discounted ‘Student Rate’ registrations are for current students only and do not include continuing education credit (CEU/PDUs)About the InstructorCaroline McGrath, LPC, NCC is a Licensed Professional Counselor, Certified Trauma-Informed Breathwork and HypnoBreathwork Facilitator, Certified Somatic Jungian Coach, and Certified TRE® Provider. She is the founder of Soul of the Lotus®, a practice devoted to somatic healing, depth psychology, and embodied transformation.  Caroline's work integrates clinical counseling, nervous system regulation, breathwork, and inner child–informed approaches to support deep, lasting change. She works with college students, young adults, and midlife women navigating anxiety, identity shifts, and life transitions.  In addition to her clinical practice, she leads professional trainings for therapists and helping professionals, as well as retreats and transformational programs for midlife women. Her teaching emphasizes experiential learning, trauma-informed practice, and practical somatic tools that clinicians can confidently integrate into their work.New workshops and trainings are added to our calendar regularly. About Waza to Kokoro

Waza to Kokoro: Hands and Heart is the Japanese Garden Training Center’s flagship program, focused on helping practitioners outside Japan create authentic, locally appropriate Japanese gardens. Through hands-on instruction and expert guidance, participants build skills in design, construction, maintenance, and preservation rooted in traditional practice. Designed for professionals working in Japanese gardens, the program also welcomes landscape designers, contractors, and students in related fields, and offers accredited continuing education through the Landscape Architecture Continuing Education System.

title: Gentle Ananda Yoga with Melissa
location: Ananda Portland Temple, 4855 SW Watson Ave, Beaverton, OR, 97005, United States
description:
This class is ideal for beginners, those recovering from injury, or anyone seeking a deeply restorative practice. It’s less about “doing” and more about “being,” with props acting as companions to guide the body into ease.

Class Atmosphere

Lighting & Ambiance: Soft, warm lighting with calming music or silence to encourage relaxation.
Pace: Slow, mindful transitions with long holds to allow the body to settle.
Focus: Creating comfort, stability, and spaciousness in each posture.

Props & Supports

Bolsters & Pillows: Used to support the spine or to cushion knees in seated poses.
Blankets: Folded for extra padding under joints or rolled to elevate hips.
Blocks: Provide height and stability in standing poses or gentle forward folds.
Straps: Assist in reaching without strain, especially in hamstring stretches or shoulder openers.
Chairs: Offer support for balance postures or seated variations.

Flow of the Class

Centering: Begin by focusing on breath awareness.
Gentle Warm-Up
Ananda Poses: supported standing poses like warrior variations with a chair or block.
Relaxation: Savasana with props.
Guided meditation with visualization

Benefits

Physical: Relieves tension, supports joints, encourages gentle mobility.
Mental: Reduces stress, cultivates mindfulness, enhances body awareness.
Emotional: Creates a safe, nurturing environment for release and renewal.

Ananda Yoga® is inherently gentle and our instructors encourage and support appropriate modifications so all bodies can participate safely. Come early to class and speak with the instructor about your needs.
$15.00 per class
$10.00 per class:  Senior discount for 60 years old +

Drop-ins welcome. Preregister and prepayment optional.

(packages must be purchased on site)

Melissa Heart has been teaching Ananda Yoga since 2012 as a certified Ananda Yoga instructor. She’s been with Ananda Portland since 2007 and has served in many capacities at the temple. Currently she serves as a member of the ministry team, manager of the temple and coordinator for Education for Life Outreach Programs.

***************************************************************************
Testimonial from Lori Arveson, student:
"I have been practicing Ananda Yoga for several years, and it has become a deeply inward and centering experience for me. The postures are held with mindful awareness, each accompanied by a silent affirmation that gently guides my attention within. As I move through the poses, my mind settles and the practice becomes a form of moving meditation.
Melissa brings a soft, grounded presence to each class. She begins by inviting us into stillness, seated in meditation with uplifting Ananda music, and gently leads us through pranayama. The class closes with a few moments of silent meditation, allowing everything to integrate. By the end of each session, I feel both deeply relaxed and quietly energized, carrying a sense of calm with me beyond the mat."
 

Review of Ananda Yoga – Beaverton OR.
From: Rick Cady - Tualatin, OR.

"As a current student of Ayurveda, I had been looking to complement my studies with a Yoga tradition that would support the ideals espoused by the ancients related to the Yoga sciences. Given that the Western model of Yoga tends toward only a focus on the physical aspects of the practice, I was happy to find a more traditional practice of Hatha Yoga through the Ananda Temple here in Beaverton, OR. Teacher Melissa Heart brings this practice to life with her unique and effective teaching style with an emphasis on being conscious and still as we move into poses, hold the pose, and come out of the pose. This practice emphasizes utilizing the poses to relax the body and be aware of our state of mind to ultimately prepare for meditation. Melissa is a gem that I am grateful to have met, as you can feel her love for the practice and desire to share it with others. On a physical level, I had been diagnosed many years ago with a Lumbar spine defect that had given me significant pain and limitations for several decades, and this practice has made me virtually pain free in about 3 months. A true miracle. I am forever grateful and will be a lifetime supporter of Melissa and Ananda Yoga."

description:
All Ananda kriyabans are invited to meditate together once a month. This is a special time of inner stillness and kriya practice for those kriyabans in the Portland area. Group meditation strengthens our practice and gives us support through other sincere souls.

Yogananda said:

"Individual and group meditation both are necessary. The former recharges the Soul with God; the latter recharges the mind with the good vibrations of the Spiritual convictions of other Souls."

and

"Group meditation is a castle which protects the new Spiritual aspirants as well as the veteran meditators. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-Realization of each member of the group by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of Spiritual magnetism.

Group meditation will hold people together, not because of the Leader’s personality, or because of musical programs and festivities, but because of the people’s own Self Realization. Then, too they would of their own accord want to get together often, to worship God on the united altar of their devotion."

Our united kriya practice can be a powerful force for change in the world!

Come for all or part of the morning, on the third Saturday of each month.

description: This course will cover the topic of disordered eating and eating disorders in children.  Family therapy treatment strategies including the Maudsley method and other approaches will be discussed.  Additional focus will be placed on ways to foster healthy eating and positive lifestyle choices in families.  This course is part of our Eating Disorder Certificate Program (https://www.lclark.edu/programs/continuing_education/certificates/eating_disorders/).Course Details & RegistrationDates: Saturday & Sunday, June 20-21, 2026, 9 a.m.-5:30 p.m., PT, OnlineInstructor: Dianne Lamberty Rogers, LMFT, CADCCurrent Students and Certificate Candidates: CECP 878-21, 1 semester hour of Graduate Continuing Education credit, $385. Individual Class: We welcome students seeking to take individual courses within the certificate program. If you have a disability that may impact your academic performance, you may request accommodations by meeting with the Office of Student Accessibility staff and submitting documentation on the Office of Student Accessibility website (/offices/student-accessibility/). Please be aware that the process for evaluation and implementation of accommodations could take 2-3 weeks, so please be in touch with the OSA as soon as possible. Email access@lclark.edu (mailto:access@lclark.edu) with any additional questions or concerns.About the Instructor  Dianne Lamberty Rogers, LMFT, CADC has been a therapist serving kids, families and adults since completing her Masters in Marriage Couple and Family Therapy at Lewis and Clark Graduate School in 2015. Dianne has specialized in working with disordered eating and body image issues, families of clients with eating disorders, and Spanish speaking families.  Dianne has worked with youth and families in school based, intensive in-home, and outpatient settings providing drug, alcohol, and mental health treatment, and also in intensive outpatient and partial hospitalization settings for eating disorders. Dianne's work has included working with incarcerated youth, DHS-involved families, and foster and adopted youth.  Dianne conducts all of her work using a trauma informed and culturally competent lens as well as a body liberation standpoint. Dianne teaches the Family Therapy in the Treatment of Eating Disorders course in the Eating Disorders Certificate Program at Lewis & Clark Graduate School. She is also a Clinical Supervisor to Lewis and Clark and other graduate interns at Youth Contact Inc.New workshops and trainings are added to our calendar regularly. description:
The Farmers Market Has Moved!
We’re now located at Clackamas Community College in Oregon City. Find us in Green Lot #1, near the corner of S Beavercreek Road and Clairmont Drive.
Click here to learn more about the new location.

About the Market
Our year‑round Farmers Market celebrates the best of our region – featuring local growers, farmers, ranchers, bakers, food producers, wineries, distilleries, cideries, and artisans
Click here for our interactive vendor map.

Summer Market Schedule (2026)
The Summer Market runs Saturdays, 9:00am–1:00pm, from May 2nd through October 31st. We operate outdoors, rain or shine, with ample parking and full ADA access.

Market Programming
We’re proud to offer a variety of free, family‑friendly programs throughout the season:
Power of Produce (POP) Club

A nationally recognized kids’ program offering weekly activities and tokens to purchase fresh produce and veggie plant starts for children ages 5–12. POP empowers kids to make healthy food choices, learn where their food comes from, and engage in hands‑on food and garden activities all summer long. Learn more.
Field‑to‑Fork Market Kitchen
Join us for cooking samples featuring seasonal produce from our vendors. Learn simple, budget‑friendly recipes and pick up tips for making the most of your market haul. Learn more.
Live Music
Enjoy local musicians every Saturday, adding a lively soundtrack to your market morning and creating a welcoming community atmosphere.
OSU Extension Master Gardeners
Visit the Master Gardener booth for expert advice on plant care, pest management, soil health, and home gardening. They’re here to help you grow with confidence.

SNAP & Double Up Food Bucks
We proudly accept SNAP/EBT, with up to a $20 Double Up Food Bucks match per market visit—made possible through grant support from Farmers Market Fund. Learn more.

Weather & Updates
The market runs rain or shine, but may close early or cancel in cases of severe weather. Visit our website for the latest updates, attending vendors, and event information.
Want weekly updates? Subscribe to our mailing list to stay connected with market news, events, and vendor highlights.

title: Fire Ceremony and Purification, Meditation: Drop-In
location: Ananda Temple in Beaverton, 4855 SW Watson Avenue, Beaverton, Oregon, 97005, United States
description:
A Vedic Fire Ceremony and Purification Ceremony is open to all on Sunday mornings at 9:00 am, followed by meditation. This is offered in the sanctuary, prior to Sunday Service, which begins at 10 am.

Details of these ceremonies can be found HERE.

Two mantras are repeated seven times, while ghee and rice are added to the fire. The ghee represents our heart's devotion and the grains of rice represent our karma that keeps us from perfect union with God. The fire is the divine light that is the source of all that is. We repeat the mantras with a recording of Swami Kriyananda chanting in Sanskrit.

The fire ceremony is followed by a Purification Ceremony and silent meditation which ends at 9:45.

All are welcome.
Gayatri Mantra
Om
Bhur bhuvah swah;
Om tat savitur varenyam
bhargo devasya dhimahi
dhiyo yo nah prachodayat.
Om
Translation:
We meditate on the Supreme Effulgence
of the three universes.
May It enlighten our consciousness.

The Mahamritunjaya Mantra
Om
Triambakam yajamahe
sugandim pushti vardhanam
urvarukam eva bhandhan
mrityor mukshiya mamritat
Swaha.
Translation:
We worship that One of divine vision
who nourishes all living beings.
May He free us from death
and grant us immortality.

title: Healthy Cross Cultural Teams - Pre K-12 (Hybrid)
location: Virtual, and Clackamas Education Service District
description: Educators need systematic ways to engage each other on how culture and race shape all aspects of their work—from curriculum and instruction to assessment, feedback, family and community relationships, and cross-cultural collaboration with colleagues.  This week-long course for school-based Pre K-12 educators will help individuals and teams examine their positionality and racial socialization through critical reflection.  Participants will explore how racial identity development and cultural literacy strengthen relationships with colleagues, students, and communities, and together build skills for disrupting inequitable systems through cross-cultural solidarity.Participants in this course will strengthen their skills around:      Understanding how our racial identity impacts our work in schools and the role of racial literacy in creating healthy identity development          Developing processes to nurture and grow principled relationships across race          Sustaining cross-racial solidarity while navigating institutional realities and resistance    Action planning to create a vision and values to help guide the work of cross-racial teams, and develop next steps to continue the work back at their sites  Course DetailsDates and Times: Monday-Friday, June 22-26, 2026In-Person: June 22, 24, 26, 2026, 9 a.m.- 4 p.m., Clackamas Education Service District, 13455 SE 97th Avenue, Clackamas, OR Virtual: June 23, 25, 2026, 9:30-11:30 a.m.Instructors: Elizabeth Denevi, PhD, and Jasmine LockeGraduate Continuing Education credit: CEED-866-21, 2 semester hours, $770Limited scholarships available to educators working in a Multnomah or Clackamas County School District, MESD, or CESD. All course texts and materials will be provided to all participants at no cost.  Course RegistrationStep 1: Follow the link below to access registration and scholarship applicationStep 2: CCE will follow up by email with credit-bearing course registration and enrollment instructionsRegister online (https://pdnetworks.soesd.k12.or.us/public/events/view-event/15508)About the InstructorsElizabeth Denevi, PhD, is an assistant clinical professor at Lewis & Clark Graduate School of Education and Counseling. She has served as a classroom teacher as well as an equity director, leadership coach, and director of professional development. She is co-author of Learning and Teaching While White: Antiracist Strategies for School Communities (with Jenna Chandler Ward) as well as Integrating Educator Well-Being, Growth, and Evaluation: Four Foundations for Leaders (with Lori Cohen), both featured titles in Routledge's Equity and Social Justice in Education series.Jasmine Locke is an equity-centered educational leader and doctoral candidate at Lewis & Clark Graduate School of Education and Counseling. Her research explores racial literacy, socialization, and the educational trajectories of students engaged in Black Student Unions. With a decade of experience as a classroom teacher, school support specialist and equity coach, she brings deep expertise in culturally responsive pedagogy, student identity development, and systems-level change. She is featured in Teach for Climate Justice: A Vision for Transforming Education, highlighting her commitment to joy as a form of resistance.New workshops and trainings are added to our calendar regularly. For the latest on professional development related to your specific interests, sign up for our mailing list! (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/4735441)

title: In Divine Friendship: A Zoom Book Study
description:
What is Divine Friendship?

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have, such as:

Strengthening one's faith
Acceleration of spiritual progress
Standing up for truth
Meditating more deeply
Responding to illness
Earning a living
Attracting a mate
Raising children
Overcoming negative self-judgments
Responding to world upheavals

Connecting all of these letters is the love, compassion, and wisdom of Swami Kriyananda, one of the leading spiritual figures of our times.

The letters describe in detail his efforts to fulfill his Guru's commission to establish spiritual communities—"would brotherhood colonies"—and offer invaluable advice to leaders everywhere on how to avoid the temptations of materialism, selfishness, and pride. A spiritual treasure that speaks to spiritual seekers at all levels.

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have

Join Surendra and friends near and far in this fascinating discussion about Yogananda's teachings on the changing consciousness of humankind across the ages.

Surendra is a member of Ananda Portland's ministry team, and has studied and lived the teachings of Yogananda while serving Ananda in Seattle, Palo Alto, India and Portland. He is also an author of 5 books of spiritual essays and poetry.

 

Register for this weekly book study below. The length of the course depends entirely on the pace set by the group. We invite you to pay a one-time fee for the course on a sliding scale.

After you register, you will be sent the Zoom link to attend the weekly discussions.

description:
Weekday mornings we offer a group meditation in the beautiful sanctuary of our temple.  Each morning is led by a different member of our ministry team with the following flow:

6:15 - doors are open

6:30 - opening prayer, chanting, reading from Whispers from Eternity by Paramhansa Yogananda

6:40 approx - silent meditation begins

6:45 - front door is locked

7:55 - 8: 00  -  meditation ends with healing prayers

 

You are able to leave at anytime if you cannot stay for the entire meditation.  We have chairs and a few blankets and cushions available but you are encouraged to bring your own meditation gear.

 

 

"Group meditation is like a castle which protects spiritual novices as well as veteran meditators against the besieging armies of delusion. Meditating together increases the degree of Self-realization of each member of the group, by the law of invisible vibratory exchange of spiritual magnetism."   Paramhansa Yogananda

title: Drawing and Painting in the Classroom (In-Person)
location: Lewis & Clark College, TBA
description: Georgia O'Keeffe once said, "I found I could say things with color and shapes that I couldn't say any other way—things I had no words for." She is not alone in feeling this way. Humans have communicated through images for thousands of years; from cave paintings to comic books, there exists a very human need to draw, paint, and make marks.  This class will cover a wide variety of drawing and painting techniques and media. There will be demonstrations, discussions, and time spent working on site in the gardens of Lewis & Clark College.  Students will leave with new skills, a small series of work, a sense of community, and a better understanding of the importance of visual communication in contemporary society.  Students will receive a materials list prior to the course start date.  Details & RegistrationDates and Time: Thursday, June 25, Monday-Thursday, June 29-July 2, 2026, 9 a.m.-3 p.m.Instructor: Kendra Larson, MFAGraduate Continuing Education Credit: CEED 852-21, 2 semester hours, $770Register Online (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/4735371)We are committed to making our events accessible to all needs and abilities. She received her MFA in Painting at University of Wisconsin, Madison and has shown her work in venues including the Whatcom Museum (Bellingham, WA), the University of Minnesota's Nash Gallery (Minneapolis, MN), Boise State University (Boise, ID), and Overture Center for the Arts (Madison, WI). Her work invites viewers to reimagine their relationship with the natural world, reignite a sense of wonder, and advocate for environmental care through the language of paint.  Her work has appeared in publications such as The Bear Deluxe and Tree Sap Magazine. Larson is a past artist in residence at Caldera (Sisters, Oregon), New Pacific Studios (Masterton, New Zealand), and Fish Factory Creative Centre of Stöðvarfjörður (Iceland). When not in the studio, she teaches at Clark College and is the Archer Gallery and Clark Art Talks Director. She is represented by Augen Gallery in Portland, OR and AMcE Creative Arts in Seattle, WA. New workshops and trainings are added to our calendar regularly. title: Applied Suicide Intervention Skills Training (ASIST) [In-Person]
location: Lewis & Clark Graduate School, South Chapel and York 107
description: The Applied Suicide Intervention Skills Training (ASIST) is an intensive, interactive and practice-dominated course for those who want to feel more comfortable, confident and competent in providing an intervention with someone who is having thoughts of suicide. This workshop will provide extensive opportunities for supported skills practice and shared participant experiences that enrich learning.After this workshop, participants will have an increased ability to:      Recognize when someone may be thinking about suicide          Provide a skilled intervention, including connect the person to further support          Guide the development of a safety plan through a collaborative, helping relationship          Consider how personal and community attitudes about suicide affect someone's openness to seek help and the caregiver's ability to provide it          Reduce suicide stigma and build confidence and capacity to provide suicide first aidWho should attend? The training is for anyone in a position of trust, including mental health and addictions professionals, school psychologists, school counselors, educators, healthcare workers, peer support and recovery specialists, housing specialists, law enforcement, faith leaders, and community volunteers.  "Prior to participating in ASIST, I was reluctant to get involved in conversations involving suicide because I felt uneasy about how to engage effectively. I walked away from this training with clear and applicable tools to enter a conversation with confidence and fearlessness, equipped to support and converse openly about suicide. It was absolutely one of the most valuable trainings I have experienced in my career."  - Counselor, Roosevelt High SchoolTraining credits are NASP and NASW-approved for Continuing Professional Development (CPD).Details & RegistrationDates and Time: Friday & Saturday, June 26-27, 2026, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m. Location: Lewis & Clark Graduate School, South Chapel and York 107Instructors: Leslie Rodgers, and Kathy Wilson-FeyCost and Credits: $350, includes 15 NASP-Approved CEUs or PDUs (12.75 NASW Credits). Alumni, Adjuncts, and GSEC Clinical Mental Health Supervisors save 20%. Register Online (https://lclark.tfaforms.net/wf1W4MQ?epid=a1aUY000002Unrl)Accessibility: We are committed to making our events accessible to all needs and abilities. When registering, please let us know your access needs. Contact us at 503-768-6040 or cce@lclark.edu (mailto:cce@lclark.edu) with questions.Please note: Discounted ‘Student Rate’ registrations are for current students only and do not include continuing education credit (CEU/PDUs)About the InstructorsLeslie Rodgers is a licensed clinical social worker and registered ASIST (Applied Suicide Intervention Skills) trainer with over 20 years experience working with children and adults in various therapeutic settings, including group homes, psychiatric hospitals, and schools. Her current work has involved implementing best practice procedures and providing staff development in student threat assessment, suicide prevention, and crisis response for school districts. She holds a BA from the University of Texas and a Masters in Social Work from Portland State University.Kathy Wilson-Fey is a registered ASIST Trainer and has clinical therapy and teaching experience in a variety of settings, including community college, community mental health, and an international university. She has 15 years of experience as a mental health specialist in public schools, where she worked with students and families, trained school staff on suicide intervention, and coordinated school support during crises. Kathy is fluent in Spanish and is committed to equity work and cultural competence. title: Gentle Ananda Yoga with Melissa
location: Ananda Portland Temple, 4855 SW Watson Ave, Beaverton, OR, 97005, United States
description:
This class is ideal for beginners, those recovering from injury, or anyone seeking a deeply restorative practice. It’s less about “doing” and more about “being,” with props acting as companions to guide the body into ease.

Class Atmosphere

Lighting & Ambiance: Soft, warm lighting with calming music or silence to encourage relaxation.
Pace: Slow, mindful transitions with long holds to allow the body to settle.
Focus: Creating comfort, stability, and spaciousness in each posture.

Props & Supports

Bolsters & Pillows: Used to support the spine or to cushion knees in seated poses.
Blankets: Folded for extra padding under joints or rolled to elevate hips.
Blocks: Provide height and stability in standing poses or gentle forward folds.
Straps: Assist in reaching without strain, especially in hamstring stretches or shoulder openers.
Chairs: Offer support for balance postures or seated variations.

Flow of the Class

Centering: Begin by focusing on breath awareness.
Gentle Warm-Up
Ananda Poses: supported standing poses like warrior variations with a chair or block.
Relaxation: Savasana with props.
Guided meditation with visualization

Benefits

Physical: Relieves tension, supports joints, encourages gentle mobility.
Mental: Reduces stress, cultivates mindfulness, enhances body awareness.
Emotional: Creates a safe, nurturing environment for release and renewal.

Ananda Yoga® is inherently gentle and our instructors encourage and support appropriate modifications so all bodies can participate safely. Come early to class and speak with the instructor about your needs.
$15.00 per class
$10.00 per class:  Senior discount for 60 years old +

Drop-ins welcome. Preregister and prepayment optional.

******************************************************************

Purchase a 10 class package and save!
(packages must be purchased on site)

$15 per drop-in / 10 class package $135, get 1 class free/$13.50 per class) good for 1 year.

Melissa Heart has been teaching Ananda Yoga since 2012 as a certified Ananda Yoga instructor. She’s been with Ananda Portland since 2007 and has served in many capacities at the temple. Currently she serves as a member of the ministry team, manager of the temple and coordinator for Education for Life Outreach Programs.

***************************************************************************
Testimonial from Lori Arveson, student:
"I have been practicing Ananda Yoga for several years, and it has become a deeply inward and centering experience for me. The postures are held with mindful awareness, each accompanied by a silent affirmation that gently guides my attention within. As I move through the poses, my mind settles and the practice becomes a form of moving meditation.
Melissa brings a soft, grounded presence to each class. She begins by inviting us into stillness, seated in meditation with uplifting Ananda music, and gently leads us through pranayama. The class closes with a few moments of silent meditation, allowing everything to integrate. By the end of each session, I feel both deeply relaxed and quietly energized, carrying a sense of calm with me beyond the mat."
 

Review of Ananda Yoga – Beaverton OR.
From: Rick Cady - Tualatin, OR.

"As a current student of Ayurveda, I had been looking to complement my studies with a Yoga tradition that would support the ideals espoused by the ancients related to the Yoga sciences. Given that the Western model of Yoga tends toward only a focus on the physical aspects of the practice, I was happy to find a more traditional practice of Hatha Yoga through the Ananda Temple here in Beaverton, OR. Teacher Melissa Heart brings this practice to life with her unique and effective teaching style with an emphasis on being conscious and still as we move into poses, hold the pose, and come out of the pose. This practice emphasizes utilizing the poses to relax the body and be aware of our state of mind to ultimately prepare for meditation. Melissa is a gem that I am grateful to have met, as you can feel her love for the practice and desire to share it with others. On a physical level, I had been diagnosed many years ago with a Lumbar spine defect that had given me significant pain and limitations for several decades, and this practice has made me virtually pain free in about 3 months. A true miracle. I am forever grateful and will be a lifetime supporter of Melissa and Ananda Yoga."

title: Body Politics (Online)
location: Online
description: As clinicians, we need to be prepared to help clients deconstruct how their bodies have been storied.  This includes raising awareness of, and challenging, the impact of societal and relational power dynamics. These dynamics impact not only our inner dialog, but the everyday realities of our lives.  This course explores how we evaluate our bodies through the lens of "unidentified others," as well as the lived experience and consequences of looks, privilege and discrimination.  Participants will consider liberation-based counseling practices to counter the objectification, commodification, power and gendering of bodies in late capitalist societies.  The focus of this course is to raise awareness of body politics in the clinical practice and creating opportunities for change through individual and relational wellbeing.  This course is part of our Eating Disorders Certificate Program (https://graduate.lclark.edu/programs/continuing_education/certificates/eating_disorders/).Course Details & RegistrationDates and Times: Saturday-Sunday, June 27-28, 2026, 9 a.m.-3:50 p.m., PT, OnlineInstructor: Krystal Marcinkiewicz, MA, LPC, LMHCCurrent Students and Certificate Candidates: CECP 837-1, 1 semester hour of Graduate Continuing Education credit, $385. Individual Class: We welcome students seeking to take individual courses within the certificate program. About the Market
Our year‑round Farmers Market celebrates the best of our region – featuring local growers, farmers, ranchers, bakers, food producers, wineries, distilleries, cideries, and artisans
Click here for our interactive vendor map.

Summer Market Schedule (2026)
The Summer Market runs Saturdays, 9:00am–1:00pm, from May 2nd through October 31st. We operate outdoors, rain or shine, with ample parking and full ADA access.

Market Programming
We’re proud to offer a variety of free, family‑friendly programs throughout the season:
Power of Produce (POP) Club

A nationally recognized kids’ program offering weekly activities and tokens to purchase fresh produce and veggie plant starts for children ages 5–12. POP empowers kids to make healthy food choices, learn where their food comes from, and engage in hands‑on food and garden activities all summer long. Learn more.
Field‑to‑Fork Market Kitchen
Join us for cooking samples featuring seasonal produce from our vendors. Learn simple, budget‑friendly recipes and pick up tips for making the most of your market haul. Learn more.
Live Music
Enjoy local musicians every Saturday, adding a lively soundtrack to your market morning and creating a welcoming community atmosphere.
OSU Extension Master Gardeners
Visit the Master Gardener booth for expert advice on plant care, pest management, soil health, and home gardening. They’re here to help you grow with confidence.

SNAP & Double Up Food Bucks
We proudly accept SNAP/EBT, with up to a $20 Double Up Food Bucks match per market visit—made possible through grant support from Farmers Market Fund. Learn more.

Weather & Updates

title: Cultural Demonstration: Kashintei Tea Ceremony
location: Kashintei Tea House, 611 SW Kingston Ave., Portland, Oregon, 97212, United States
description:
Tea Ceremony taking place in the Tea Garden. Photo by Jonathan Ley.

Portland Japanese Garden will offer a free public demonstration of Chado, the Way of Tea, in the Kashintei Tea House (in the Tea Garden) from 1:15 – 2:15pm. The Way of Tea is intrinsically linked to Japanese gardens and understanding the kokoro (heart) of Japanese gardening.

Kashintei (literally “Flower-Heart Room”) is the name of the authentic Tea House that sits in the heart of our Tea Garden. The structure was made in Japan, shipped in pieces, and reassembled in the Garden. Tea houses are composed of several strictly defined spaces: the anteroom [mizuya], where the utensils for the ceremony are readied beforehand; the sitting room [zashiki], where the tea ceremony is performed; the alcove [tokonoma] where flowers and a calligraphy scroll are displayed.  Four-and-a-half tatami mats, which are the standard dimensions of a traditional tea house, cover the floor.

Photo by Tyler Quinn.

Two mantras are repeated seven times, while ghee and rice are added to the fire. title: In Divine Friendship: A Zoom Book Study
description:
What is Divine Friendship?

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have, such as:

Strengthening one's faith
Acceleration of spiritual progress
Standing up for truth
Meditating more deeply
Responding to illness
Earning a living
Attracting a mate
Raising children
Overcoming negative self-judgments
Responding to world upheavals

Connecting all of these letters is the love, compassion, and wisdom of Swami Kriyananda, one of the leading spiritual figures of our times.

The letters describe in detail his efforts to fulfill his Guru's commission to establish spiritual communities—"would brotherhood colonies"—and offer invaluable advice to leaders everywhere on how to avoid the temptations of materialism, selfishness, and pride. A spiritual treasure that speaks to spiritual seekers at all levels.

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have

title: Teacher's Workshop at Tule Lake
location: Oregon
description:
Join the Japanese American Museum of Oregon for a 6-day teacher workshop in Portland and at the Tule Lake Monument. This in-depth learning experience includes travel from Portland to the Tule Lake area outside of Klamath Falls, Oregon. Participants will gain knowledge of Japanese American history in Oregon, a variety of resources for teaching Japanese American history in the classroom, and the opportunity to hear directly from Japanese American community members, scholars, and local educators about the forced removal and incarceration Japanese Americans during World War II.

Teaching Japanese American History: A Place-Based Educator WorkshopJuly 1-6, 2026Open to K-12 teachers in Oregon and WashingtonApplications due Friday, May 1

Apply Here

The Japanese American Museum of Oregon (JAMO) is accepting applications from Oregon and Washington educators to participate in a 6-day teacher workshop, entitled “Teaching Japanese American History: A Place-Based Educator Workshop,” which will take place July 1-6, 2026.

The first portion of the workshop will take place in Portland, Oregon at the Japanese American Museum of Oregon, July 1-3. During this portion, participants will dive into the history of Portland’s Nihonmachi (Japantown), engage in workshop sessions about effective teaching practices, and get introduced to a variety of resources for teaching Japanese American history in the classroom.

During the second portion of the workshop, participants will attend and support the 2026 Tule Lake Pilgrimage, July 3-6 (transportation to and from Klamath Falls, Oregon is provided). The annual pilgrimage, organized by the Tule Lake Committee, is a gathering of incarceration survivors, their descendants, and allies to honor the experience of Japanese Americans through educational sessions, tours, and community building. Participants will hear from Japanese American community members, scholars, and local educators about the forced removal and incarceration of over 125,000 Japanese Americans from the West Coast during World War II.

A group of 8 educators (K-12) will be selected to participate. Priority will be given to Oregon educators, but Washington educators are also welcome to apply.

The application period ends on Friday, May 1, 2026. Successful applicants will be notified by May 8th, 2026.

Introduction

The WWII incarceration of Japanese Americans was a period of history when over 110,000 people, two-thirds of them American citizens, were forcibly removed from their homes by Executive Order 9066 and placed in confinement sites without due process of law. Anti-Asian racism combined with tensions from the attack on Pearl Harbor caused the loyalty of Japanese Americans to be put into question. The government claimed that the incarceration was a military necessity, but a Congressional investigation over 30 years later found that it was motivated by “race prejudice, war hysteria, and a failure of political leadership.” Tule Lake, in northern California, is one of the ten US concentration camps where Japanese Americans from the West Coast were incarcerated.

Tule Lake opened May 26, 1942, detaining persons of Japanese descent removed from western Washington, Oregon and Northern California. With a peak population of 18,700, Tule Lake was the largest of the camps – the only one converted into a maximum-security segregation center, ruled under martial law and occupied by the Army. Tule Lake was the last to close, on March 28, 1946. Thanks to the preservation and advocacy work of the Tule Lake Committee, the site was designated a National Historic Landmark in 2006 and became a National Monument in 2008.

More information at nps.gov/tule and tulelake.org

Workshop

The teacher workshop will be led by Japanese American Museum of Oregon staff. Workshop will occur from July 1-6, 2026. Acceptees are expected to participate for the duration of the workshop and pilgrimage.

Draft schedule:

Wednesday, July 1: Travel to Portland, Oregon. Afternoon workshop sessions.

Thursday, July 2: Full day of workshop sessions.

Friday, July 3 – Monday, July 6: Participants will join the Tule Lake Pilgrimage. Participants will attend educational sessions and provide some volunteer support for the pilgrimage.

Monday, July 6: Tule Lake Pilgrimage ends. Travel via bus from Klamath Falls to Portland.

Travel, Lodging, & Meals

Participants are expected to make their way to Portland, Oregon on Wednesday, July 1st. The Japanese American Museum of Oregon will provide lodging at a nearby hotel for participants traveling from out of town. Most meals will be provided by JAMO or the Tule Lake Pilgrimage for the duration of the workshop and pilgrimage.

Lodging during the pilgrimage and transportation between Portland and Klamath Falls, Oregon is provided as part of the pilgrimage experience.

Stipend

Participants will receive a $500 stipend to help offset any transportation or associated costs upon completion of the workshop.

2026 Tule Lake Pilgrimage

Participants will be automatically registered for the Tule Lake Pilgrimage. Tule Lake Pilgrimage registration fees and registration logistics will be covered by the workshop. Registration for the 2026 Tule Lake Pilgrimage has already closed to the public so additional family members will not be able to attend.

More information at https://www.tulelake.org/pilgrimage

Workshop Team

Hanako Wakatsuki-Chong, Executive Director, Japanese American Museum of Oregon

Hanako Wakatsuki-Chong is the Executive Director of the Japanese American Museum of Oregon in Portland, professionally trained as a public historian, political scientist, and museologist. She holds a BA in History and BS in Political Science from Boise State University, as well as an MA in Museum Studies from Johns Hopkins University, where she serves as an adjunct faculty member for their Krieger School of Arts and Sciences Museum Studies and Cultural Heritage Management Programs.

For 17 years, Hanako worked for state and federal agencies at the Idaho State Historical Society, the US Navy, the National Park Service, and the White House Office of the Chief of Staff; holding roles as Interpretive Specialist, Education Specialist, Chief of Interpretation and Education, Superintendent, and Policy Advisor throughout her government career.

Elissa Dingus, Director of Education and Engagement, Japanese American Museum of Oregon

Elissa spent 12 years as an elementary school teacher in the Portland, Oregon metro area, where she developed social studies curricula that expanded the focus beyond Oregon’s well-known white settler colonial past in order to make space for the less frequently told histories of marginalized groups in Oregon. She was awarded the 2017 Oregon Elementary Social Studies Teacher of the Year Award and the 2019 Lewis & Clark MAT Alumni Teacher of the Year Award. She is now the Director of Education and Engagement at the Japanese American Museum of Oregon where she facilitates educational programming at the museum to connect student groups, educators, and the general public with Japanese American history.

title: Gentle Ananda Yoga with Melissa
location: Ananda Portland Temple, 4855 SW Watson Ave, Beaverton, OR, 97005, United States
description:
This class is ideal for beginners, those recovering from injury, or anyone seeking a deeply restorative practice. It’s less about “doing” and more about “being,” with props acting as companions to guide the body into ease.

Class Atmosphere

Lighting & Ambiance: Soft, warm lighting with calming music or silence to encourage relaxation.
Pace: Slow, mindful transitions with long holds to allow the body to settle.
Focus: Creating comfort, stability, and spaciousness in each posture.

Props & Supports

Bolsters & Pillows: Used to support the spine or to cushion knees in seated poses.
Blankets: Folded for extra padding under joints or rolled to elevate hips.
Blocks: Provide height and stability in standing poses or gentle forward folds.
Straps: Assist in reaching without strain, especially in hamstring stretches or shoulder openers.
Chairs: Offer support for balance postures or seated variations.

Flow of the Class

Centering: Begin by focusing on breath awareness.
Gentle Warm-Up
Ananda Poses: supported standing poses like warrior variations with a chair or block.
Relaxation: Savasana with props.
Guided meditation with visualization

Benefits

Physical: Relieves tension, supports joints, encourages gentle mobility.
Mental: Reduces stress, cultivates mindfulness, enhances body awareness.
Emotional: Creates a safe, nurturing environment for release and renewal.

Ananda Yoga® is inherently gentle and our instructors encourage and support appropriate modifications so all bodies can participate safely. Come early to class and speak with the instructor about your needs.
$15.00 per class

Drop-ins welcome. Preregister and prepayment optional.

Melissa Heart has been teaching Ananda Yoga since 2012 as a certified Ananda Yoga instructor. She’s been with Ananda Portland since 2007 and has served in many capacities at the temple. Currently she serves as a member of the ministry team, manager of the temple and coordinator for Education for Life Outreach Programs.

***************************************************************************
Testimonial from Lori Arveson, student:
"I have been practicing Ananda Yoga for several years, and it has become a deeply inward and centering experience for me. The postures are held with mindful awareness, each accompanied by a silent affirmation that gently guides my attention within. As I move through the poses, my mind settles and the practice becomes a form of moving meditation.
Melissa brings a soft, grounded presence to each class. She begins by inviting us into stillness, seated in meditation with uplifting Ananda music, and gently leads us through pranayama. The class closes with a few moments of silent meditation, allowing everything to integrate. By the end of each session, I feel both deeply relaxed and quietly energized, carrying a sense of calm with me beyond the mat."
 

Review of Ananda Yoga – Beaverton OR.
From: Rick Cady - Tualatin, OR.

"As a current student of Ayurveda, I had been looking to complement my studies with a Yoga tradition that would support the ideals espoused by the ancients related to the Yoga sciences. Given that the Western model of Yoga tends toward only a focus on the physical aspects of the practice, I was happy to find a more traditional practice of Hatha Yoga through the Ananda Temple here in Beaverton, OR. Teacher Melissa Heart brings this practice to life with her unique and effective teaching style with an emphasis on being conscious and still as we move into poses, hold the pose, and come out of the pose. This practice emphasizes utilizing the poses to relax the body and be aware of our state of mind to ultimately prepare for meditation. Melissa is a gem that I am grateful to have met, as you can feel her love for the practice and desire to share it with others. On a physical level, I had been diagnosed many years ago with a Lumbar spine defect that had given me significant pain and limitations for several decades, and this practice has made me virtually pain free in about 3 months. A true miracle. I am forever grateful and will be a lifetime supporter of Melissa and Ananda Yoga."

Two mantras are repeated seven times, while ghee and rice are added to the fire. description:
Photo Courtesy of Oregon Koto Kai

Enjoy a free koto performance by Oregon Koto-Kai at 1:15pm at the Cathy Rudd Cultural Corner in the Jordan Schnitzer Japanese Arts Learning Center.

About the Koto

The standard Koto is a thirteen-string plucked zither introduced to Japan in the 7th century. It has been part of the Gagaku court ensemble for over a thousand years, becoming popular among the merchant classes in the Edo period (1600-1868). An important member of the traditional Sankyoku ensemble, along with the three-string Shamisen and Shakuhachi (bamboo flute), the Koto developed further in a solo capacity, eventually becoming one of Japan’s most prominent musical instruments. Today, its varied repertoire and wide range of playing techniques provide a rich palette of sound textures, making the Koto appealing to audiences worldwide. Learn more about Koto.

Oregon Koto-Kai

Oregon Koto-Kai is a group passionate about the Japanese koto, a 13-stringed zither with over 1000 years of history. Founded by Mitsuki Dazai in February 2012, the ensemble performed its first concert in Portland, Oregon. Since then, they have performed throughout the state at venues like the Portland Japanese Garden, Portland Rose Festival, and Oregon Shakespeare Festival in Ashland. Their mission is to introduce Japanese koto music to the broader community by providing concerts and lessons. They collaborate with local musicians, improve players’ skills, and contribute to the cultural

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have, such as:

Strengthening one's faith
Acceleration of spiritual progress
Standing up for truth
Meditating more deeply
Responding to illness
Earning a living
Attracting a mate
Raising children
Overcoming negative self-judgments
Responding to world upheavals

title: Cultivating Spaciousness and Abundance: Courage to Lead® for Sustainable Growth (Online)
location: Online
description: As leaders we are often called to come from a place of perpetual productivity, bottomless capacity, always giving and always "on". Yet the wholeness of who we are requires periods of reflection, receiving and renewal. When we do not honor this necessary balance, the wisdom of our hearts is harder to hear.What's growing in your life? What needs to be nourished for further growth? What do you want to prune or clear out?How do we listen to and honor what we need to be whole and in balance amid the demands and desires of an abundant life, in a way that allows for spaciousness, authenticity and joy?How do we tend to the garden of our lives and our work so that we can receive what we need to flourish?  Held during a time of peak growth and seasonal abundance, this Courage to Lead® two-day workshop invites us into spacious time for reflection, connection, and inner growth.Together we will…      Pause and cultivate our capacity to be present          Meaningfully engage with ourselves, others and nature with spaciousness and care          Take stock of our relationship to abundance and consider intentional paths of growth and clearing          Develop skills for holding meaningful conversations and building relational trust          Explore reflective and creative practices including the SoulCollage (https://soulcollage.com/about/)® method, an expressive arts practice used as a tool for accessing personal and archetypal wisdom      To ensure your SoulCollage (https://soulcollage.com/about/)® materials packet arrives before the workshop, register by June 24.Details & RegistrationDates and Times: Thursday-Friday, July 9-10, 2026, 9:30 a.m.-2:30 p.m. PT, OnlineFacilitator: Matsya Siosal, and Rafaela Steen, LCSWRegistration: $225. title: Understanding, Exploring, and Supporting Perimenopause and Menopause Experiences in The Therapy Room (In-Person)
location: Lewis & Clark Graduate School
description: Menopause and perimenopause can magnify emotional and psychological distress—often showing up as irritability, mood shifts, anxiety, depression, grief, self-doubt, brain fog, and heightened emotional insecurity. These experiences can disrupt relationships, work functioning, and a client's sense of identity and self-efficacy. Many clients report little preparation, limited validation, and inconsistent guidance on what to expect or how to cope.  This skills-based training equips clinicians and helping professionals with practical, trauma-informed, and culturally responsive tools to support clients who are navigating menopause-related mental health and life-transition stress.  Presenter Audrianna J. Gurr, LPC, CADCI, mental health clinician and author of I'm Still Hot! Surviving and Thriving in Your Mental Health During Menopause, will guide participants through a framework for identifying common emotional patterns, normalizing the experience without minimizing it, and selecting concrete interventions that can be used immediately in session.Following this training, participants will have the ability to:      Identify common emotional and psychological experiences that may intensify during perimenopause/menopause and differentiate them from other clinical presentations          Apply a brief session-ready framework for validating menopause-related distress while supporting client agency and self-compassion          Use the "Three Tiers" expectations tool to reduce anxiety-driven over-control and support realistic planning.           Teach assertiveness and boundary-setting skills using a "Personal Bill of Rights" lens to strengthen self-advocacy and relational functioning.          Adapt interventions with attention to equity and diversity, including how gender socialization, culture, and systemic barriers shape help-seeking, access to care, and empowerment during midlife transitions. title: Gentle Ananda Yoga with Melissa
location: Ananda Portland Temple, 4855 SW Watson Ave, Beaverton, OR, 97005, United States
description:
This class is ideal for beginners, those recovering from injury, or anyone seeking a deeply restorative practice. It’s less about “doing” and more about “being,” with props acting as companions to guide the body into ease.

Class Atmosphere

Lighting & Ambiance: Soft, warm lighting with calming music or silence to encourage relaxation.
Pace: Slow, mindful transitions with long holds to allow the body to settle.
Focus: Creating comfort, stability, and spaciousness in each posture.

Props & Supports

Bolsters & Pillows: Used to support the spine or to cushion knees in seated poses.
Blankets: Folded for extra padding under joints or rolled to elevate hips.
Blocks: Provide height and stability in standing poses or gentle forward folds.
Straps: Assist in reaching without strain, especially in hamstring stretches or shoulder openers.
Chairs: Offer support for balance postures or seated variations.

Flow of the Class

Centering: Begin by focusing on breath awareness.
Gentle Warm-Up
Ananda Poses: supported standing poses like warrior variations with a chair or block.
Relaxation: Savasana with props.
Guided meditation with visualization

Benefits

Physical: Relieves tension, supports joints, encourages gentle mobility.
Mental: Reduces stress, cultivates mindfulness, enhances body awareness.
Emotional: Creates a safe, nurturing environment for release and renewal.

Ananda Yoga® is inherently gentle and our instructors encourage and support appropriate modifications so all bodies can participate safely. Come early to class and speak with the instructor about your needs.
$15.00 per class
$10.00 per class:  Senior discount for 60 years old +

Drop-ins welcome. Preregister and prepayment optional.

******************************************************************

Purchase a 10 class package and save!
(packages must be purchased on site)

Melissa Heart has been teaching Ananda Yoga since 2012 as a certified Ananda Yoga instructor. She’s been with Ananda Portland since 2007 and has served in many capacities at the temple. Currently she serves as a member of the ministry team, manager of the temple and coordinator for Education for Life Outreach Programs.

***************************************************************************
Testimonial from Lori Arveson, student:
"I have been practicing Ananda Yoga for several years, and it has become a deeply inward and centering experience for me. The postures are held with mindful awareness, each accompanied by a silent affirmation that gently guides my attention within. As I move through the poses, my mind settles and the practice becomes a form of moving meditation.
Melissa brings a soft, grounded presence to each class. She begins by inviting us into stillness, seated in meditation with uplifting Ananda music, and gently leads us through pranayama. The class closes with a few moments of silent meditation, allowing everything to integrate. By the end of each session, I feel both deeply relaxed and quietly energized, carrying a sense of calm with me beyond the mat."
 

Review of Ananda Yoga – Beaverton OR.
From: Rick Cady - Tualatin, OR.

"As a current student of Ayurveda, I had been looking to complement my studies with a Yoga tradition that would support the ideals espoused by the ancients related to the Yoga sciences. Given that the Western model of Yoga tends toward only a focus on the physical aspects of the practice, I was happy to find a more traditional practice of Hatha Yoga through the Ananda Temple here in Beaverton, OR. Teacher Melissa Heart brings this practice to life with her unique and effective teaching style with an emphasis on being conscious and still as we move into poses, hold the pose, and come out of the pose. This practice emphasizes utilizing the poses to relax the body and be aware of our state of mind to ultimately prepare for meditation. Melissa is a gem that I am grateful to have met, as you can feel her love for the practice and desire to share it with others. On a physical level, I had been diagnosed many years ago with a Lumbar spine defect that had given me significant pain and limitations for several decades, and this practice has made me virtually pain free in about 3 months. A true miracle. I am forever grateful and will be a lifetime supporter of Melissa and Ananda Yoga."

title: Body Politics (Online)
location: Online
description: As clinicians, we need to be prepared to help clients deconstruct how their bodies have been storied.  This includes raising awareness of, and challenging, the impact of societal and relational power dynamics. These dynamics impact not only our inner dialog, but the everyday realities of our lives.  This course explores how we evaluate our bodies through the lens of "unidentified others," as well as the lived experience and consequences of looks, privilege and discrimination.  Participants will consider liberation-based counseling practices to counter the objectification, commodification, power and gendering of bodies in late capitalist societies.  The focus of this course is to raise awareness of body politics in the clinical practice and creating opportunities for change through individual and relational wellbeing.  This course is part of our Eating Disorders Certificate Program (https://graduate.lclark.edu/programs/continuing_education/certificates/eating_disorders/).Course Details & RegistrationDates and Times: Saturday & Sunday, July 11 & 12, 2026, 9 a.m.-5:30 p.m., PT, OnlineInstructor: Krystal Marcinkiewicz, MA, LPC, LMHCCurrent Students and Certificate Candidates: CECP 837-2, 1 semester hour of Graduate Continuing Education credit, $385. Individual Class: We welcome students seeking to take individual courses within the certificate program. Drawing from an integrative feminist approach, her work is grounded in person-centered values, emphasizing authentic connection, and collaborative engagement. title: Fire Ceremony and Purification, Meditation: Drop-In
location: Ananda Temple in Beaverton, 4855 SW Watson Avenue, Beaverton, Oregon, 97005, United States
description:
A Vedic Fire Ceremony and Purification Ceremony is open to all on Sunday mornings at 9:00 am, followed by meditation. This is offered in the sanctuary, prior to Sunday Service, which begins at 10 am.

Details of these ceremonies can be found HERE.

Two mantras are repeated seven times, while ghee and rice are added to the fire. The ghee represents our heart's devotion and the grains of rice represent our karma that keeps us from perfect union with God. The fire is the divine light that is the source of all that is. We repeat the mantras with a recording of Swami Kriyananda chanting in Sanskrit.

The fire ceremony is followed by a Purification Ceremony and silent meditation which ends at 9:45.

All are welcome.
Gayatri Mantra
Om
Bhur bhuvah swah;
Om tat savitur varenyam
bhargo devasya dhimahi
dhiyo yo nah prachodayat.
Om
Translation:
We meditate on the Supreme Effulgence
of the three universes.
May It enlighten our consciousness.

The Mahamritunjaya Mantra
Om
Triambakam yajamahe
sugandim pushti vardhanam
urvarukam eva bhandhan
mrityor mukshiya mamritat
Swaha.
Translation:
We worship that One of divine vision
who nourishes all living beings.
May He free us from death
and grant us immortality.

title: In Divine Friendship: A Zoom Book Study
description:
What is Divine Friendship?

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have, such as:

Strengthening one's faith
Acceleration of spiritual progress
Standing up for truth
Meditating more deeply
Responding to illness
Earning a living
Attracting a mate
Raising children
Overcoming negative self-judgments
Responding to world upheavals

Connecting all of these letters is the love, compassion, and wisdom of Swami Kriyananda, one of the leading spiritual figures of our times.

The letters describe in detail his efforts to fulfill his Guru's commission to establish spiritual communities—"would brotherhood colonies"—and offer invaluable advice to leaders everywhere on how to avoid the temptations of materialism, selfishness, and pride. A spiritual treasure that speaks to spiritual seekers at all levels.

This extraordinary book of nearly 250 letters, written over a 30-year period by Swami Kriyananda, responds to practically any concern a spiritual seeker might have

Join Surendra and friends near and far in this fascinating discussion about Yogananda's teachings on the changing consciousness of humankind across the ages.

Surendra is a member of Ananda Portland's ministry team, and has studied and lived the teachings of Yogananda while serving Ananda in Seattle, Palo Alto, India and Portland. He is also an author of 5 books of spiritual essays and poetry.

 

Register for this weekly book study below. The length of the course depends entirely on the pace set by the group. We invite you to pay a one-time fee for the course on a sliding scale.

After you register, you will be sent the Zoom link to attend the weekly discussions.

title: Gentle Ananda Yoga with Melissa
location: Ananda Portland Temple, 4855 SW Watson Ave, Beaverton, OR, 97005, United States
description:
This class is ideal for beginners, those recovering from injury, or anyone seeking a deeply restorative practice. It’s less about “doing” and more about “being,” with props acting as companions to guide the body into ease.

Class Atmosphere

Lighting & Ambiance: Soft, warm lighting with calming music or silence to encourage relaxation.
Pace: Slow, mindful transitions with long holds to allow the body to settle.
Focus: Creating comfort, stability, and spaciousness in each posture.

Props & Supports

Bolsters & Pillows: Used to support the spine or to cushion knees in seated poses.
Blankets: Folded for extra padding under joints or rolled to elevate hips.
Blocks: Provide height and stability in standing poses or gentle forward folds.
Straps: Assist in reaching without strain, especially in hamstring stretches or shoulder openers.
Chairs: Offer support for balance postures or seated variations.

Flow of the Class

Centering: Begin by focusing on breath awareness.
Gentle Warm-Up
Ananda Poses: supported standing poses like warrior variations with a chair or block.
Relaxation: Savasana with props.
Guided meditation with visualization

Benefits

Physical: Relieves tension, supports joints, encourages gentle mobility.
Mental: Reduces stress, cultivates mindfulness, enhances body awareness.
Emotional: Creates a safe, nurturing environment for release and renewal.

Ananda Yoga® is inherently gentle and our instructors encourage and support appropriate modifications so all bodies can participate safely. Come early to class and speak with the instructor about your needs.
$15.00 per class
$10.00 per class:  Senior discount for 60 years old +

Drop-ins welcome. Preregister and prepayment optional.

******************************************************************

Purchase a 10 class package and save!
(packages must be purchased on site)

$15 per drop-in / 10 class package $135, get 1 class free/$13.50 per class) good for 1 year.

$10 Senior rate (10 class package $90, get 1 class free/ $9.00 per class) good for 1 year.

Melissa Heart has been teaching Ananda Yoga since 2012 as a certified Ananda Yoga instructor. She’s been with Ananda Portland since 2007 and has served in many capacities at the temple. Currently she serves as a member of the ministry team, manager of the temple and coordinator for Education for Life Outreach Programs.

***************************************************************************
Testimonial from Lori Arveson, student:
"I have been practicing Ananda Yoga for several years, and it has become a deeply inward and centering experience for me. The postures are held with mindful awareness, each accompanied by a silent affirmation that gently guides my attention within. As I move through the poses, my mind settles and the practice becomes a form of moving meditation.
Melissa brings a soft, grounded presence to each class. She begins by inviting us into stillness, seated in meditation with uplifting Ananda music, and gently leads us through pranayama. The class closes with a few moments of silent meditation, allowing everything to integrate. By the end of each session, I feel both deeply relaxed and quietly energized, carrying a sense of calm with me beyond the mat."
 

Review of Ananda Yoga – Beaverton OR.
From: Rick Cady - Tualatin, OR.

"As a current student of Ayurveda, I had been looking to complement my studies with a Yoga tradition that would support the ideals espoused by the ancients related to the Yoga sciences. Given that the Western model of Yoga tends toward only a focus on the physical aspects of the practice, I was happy to find a more traditional practice of Hatha Yoga through the Ananda Temple here in Beaverton, OR. Teacher Melissa Heart brings this practice to life with her unique and effective teaching style with an emphasis on being conscious and still as we move into poses, hold the pose, and come out of the pose. This practice emphasizes utilizing the poses to relax the body and be aware of our state of mind to ultimately prepare for meditation. Melissa is a gem that I am grateful to have met, as you can feel her love for the practice and desire to share it with others. On a physical level, I had been diagnosed many years ago with a Lumbar spine defect that had given me significant pain and limitations for several decades, and this practice has made me virtually pain free in about 3 months. A true miracle. I am forever grateful and will be a lifetime supporter of Melissa and Ananda Yoga."

title: Cultural Demonstration: Kashintei Tea Ceremony
location: Kashintei Tea House, 611 SW Kingston Ave., Portland, Oregon, 97212, United States
description:
Tea Ceremony taking place in the Tea Garden. Photo by Jonathan Ley.

Portland Japanese Garden will offer a free public demonstration of Chado, the Way of Tea, in the Kashintei Tea House (in the Tea Garden) from 1:15 – 2:15pm. The Way of Tea is intrinsically linked to Japanese gardens and understanding the kokoro (heart) of Japanese gardening.

Kashintei (literally “Flower-Heart Room”) is the name of the authentic Tea House that sits in the heart of our Tea Garden. The structure was made in Japan, shipped in pieces, and reassembled in the Garden. Tea houses are composed of several strictly defined spaces: the anteroom [mizuya], where the utensils for the ceremony are readied beforehand; the sitting room [zashiki], where the tea ceremony is performed; the alcove [tokonoma] where flowers and a calligraphy scroll are displayed.  Four-and-a-half tatami mats, which are the standard dimensions of a traditional tea house, cover the floor.

Photo by Tyler Quinn.
